result.funder_system:
ACS Petroleum Research Fund (ACS PRF) — an endowed fund managed by the American Chemical Society, administered by the ACS Research Grants Office in Washington DC. Four research mechanisms share ONE application machinery, one portal, one deadline and one review calendar; only eligibility, dollar amount and a couple of required statements differ.

Mechanisms (funder's own figures, Sept 2026):
- ND (New Directions) — $125,000 / 2 yrs, ~75 awards/yr. Established faculty in Ph.D.-granting departments, moving into a genuinely new direction. Open to PIs in 50+ countries.
- DNI (Doctoral New Investigator) — $110,000 / 2 yrs, ~75 awards/yr. US only; within first 3 years of first Assistant Professor appointment; Ph.D.-granting department.
- UR (Undergraduate Research) — $70,000 / 3 yrs, ~25 awards/yr. Faculty in non-doctoral departments (incl. US community colleges).
- UNI (Undergraduate New Investigator) — $55,000 / 2 yrs, ~25 awards/yr. Non-doctoral departments, within first 5 years of first appointment.
- Since 2024, departments of successful UR and UNI applicants are invited to compete for a $25,000 supplement.

Framing that matters for an applicant: PRF is explicitly SEED money for work you have NOT published on and have NOT been funded for. "ACS PRF grants are intended as seed money to enable an investigator to initiate a new research direction. The investigator should not have published or received financial support from another funding agency for the proposed research topic." Scope is restricted by the 1944 Trust to the "petroleum field" — "petroleum, natural gas, coal, shale, tar sands and like materials" — but the funder states it funds much sustainability/green-chemistry work (methane and CO2 upgrading, catalysis on petroleum-derived substrates). Fundamental research only; applied research and methods/device development are out of scope. ACS membership is NOT required and is not a factor. No overhead/indirect costs are allowed. Patents arising must be dedicated to the public royalty-free.

Hard structural constraint people miss: a PI may hold only ONE active PRF grant, and may not apply while holding one (including during a no-cost extension); and only one proposal per committee meeting.

TOOLING NOTE: acs.org serves an empty body to plain fetch and blocks curl at the Imperva/Incapsula edge; everything below came from a rendering browser against the funder's own pages, plus PDF text extracted in-browser. A subset of PRF pages currently return a genuine ACS 403 "This page is forbidden" even in the browser (undergraduate-research-grants.html, reviewers.html, contact.html, annual-report.html, salesforce-registration-help.html, uni-ur-faq.html, and acs.org's own search). For those I used the funder's own public knowledge base at prfgrant.acs.org/pkb and the funder's Salesforce site, and said so per field. cen.acs.org returns HTTP 406 to both plain fetch and the rendering browser, so C&EN items are via search index only.
result.submission_portal:
**Portal: the ACS PRF Portal (Salesforce-based) — https://prfgrant.acs.org/s/** (the funder's older pages also refer to it as www.acsprf.org). Proposal support: PRFsupport@acs.org, Mon–Fri 8:30 AM–5:00 PM ET.

**THE HIDDEN LONG-LEAD ITEM — pre-registration. You cannot even enter the submission portal until PRF approves you.** The funder's own instruction page (https://prfgrant.my.salesforce-sites.com/PRFPreRegistrationInstructions) states: "You cannot enter or proceed in the Proposal Submission Portal until Step 2 is reviewed and approved." Approval takes "Within 1–2 business days" — but it is a human approval step, so it must not be left to deadline week. The acs.org guidance (per search index; that page 403s) says applicants "must complete their Registration well in advance of the competition deadline."

Three steps:
1. **ACS ID** (~5–10 min). Free. You do NOT need to be an ACS member. PRF's own knowledge base: "You do not need to be an ACS Member to obtain the ACS User ID." Creating it assigns an ACS Customer/Member Number, which the pre-registration form requires.
2. **PRF pre-registration form** — https://prfgrant.acs.org/register/s/ (<5 min). Requires an institutional email: "Personal email addresses (Gmail, Yahoo, etc.) will not be accepted." You pick a role: **Principal Investigator** (submitting your own application) or **Grant Officer** (submitting on behalf of a PI / managing multiple submissions / managing an existing grant). You get an "Under Review" email.
3. **Approval email**, then log in at https://prfgrant.acs.org/s/ with ACS ID credentials.

Why pre-registration exists (PRF knowledge base, "Pre-registration" article, Mar 2023): "PRF implemented a Pre-Registration process in late 2021. Pre-registration is required to prevent issues with ACS IDs and creation of duplicate contact records in the PRF system."

**Second long-lead item — your research/grants office.** The application collects Grant Officer and Institutional Endorsing Official contact details, and a signature sheet must be signed by the PI, the co-PI (if any) AND an authorised institutional official — explicitly "not the Department Chair" — in TWO places on the sheet. Sequence inside the portal: fill the web form → "Download for Signatures" → obtain signatures → upload the signed PDF as file type "Signature Sheet" → Validate Application → Submit Application. The funder warns: "once the signed form is uploaded, changes cannot be made to the application or signature sheet" (a red "Cancel Signature" button reverses this if you need to edit). The same page also states "All DocuSign electronic signatures must be completed, and the application must be validated before submitting the proposal" — the page carries both the DocuSign route and the download/sign/upload route.

**No grace, no fixes after the bell:** "All proposals must be received in complete and final form by the deadline… No late submissions, additions, or document substitutions are allowed after the deadline."

Not Grants.gov, not ProposalCentral, not Research.gov — PRF runs its own portal. No SAM.gov/UEI/eRA Commons equivalent is required.
result.deadline_structure:
**Two fixed windows a year, identical across all four mechanisms (ND, DNI, UR, UNI) — and the same date for new and resubmitted proposals.** Not rolling, not per-solicitation.

Dates the funder publishes right now (verbatim from acs.org/funding/grants/petroleum-research-fund.html and each programme page, read 18 Sept 2026):

> "We are currently accepting proposals for ND, DNI, UR, or UNI grant programs to be considered at the May 2027 ACS PRF Committee Meeting. All proposals are due by 5:00 pm ET Friday, October 9, 2026."

> "Note: The Spring Submission window will be from Monday, February 15, 2027, to Friday, March 12, 2027."

The fall 2026 window opened Monday, 14 September 2026. The programme comparison table at acs.org/funding/grants/petroleum-research-fund/programs.html lists "5:00 PM ET, October 9, 2026" against all four of ND, DNI, UR and UNI.

**The recurring pattern (this is the durable rule; the dates above are this year's instance):**
- Fall window ≈ mid-September → early/mid-October. Reviewed at the **May Committee meeting of the FOLLOWING year**. Earliest award start **1 July**.
- Spring window ≈ mid-February → mid-March. Reviewed at the **October Committee meeting of the SAME year**. Earliest award start **1 January of the following year**.

Funder's own words (ND Application Instructions PDF, Rev 02/2024): "Proposals submitted in February-March will be considered at the October PRF Committee meeting; submissions in September-October will be considered in May of the next year."

And on start dates (FAQ): "For proposals to be considered in October, the earliest start date is January 1 of the following year. For proposals to be considered in May, the earliest start date is July 1. If you are unsure when a proposal will be considered, this is noted in the footer of the application form."

Budget-year mechanics that constrain your requested start date: the PRF budget year runs 1 September – 31 August. Every budget period must END on 31 August and be at least 12 months long, and a start date must be the first day of a month. So an early start simply makes Year 1 longer than 12 months.

Third-party drift warning, as a live example: Duke's research-funding listing (researchfunding.duke.edu/acs-petroleum-research-fund, posted 4 June 2026) carries the correct deadlines (10/9/2026 and 3/12/2027) but lists ND at "$110,000 over 2 years" — the funder's own ND page says $125,000. Always take the dollar figure from acs.org, not from an aggregator.
result.months_submission_to_award:
**~7 months deadline → funding decision; ~8 months → ACS Board approval; ~9 months → earliest money.** This is a slow funder by design — plan a full academic year.

Worked example for the cycle now open:
- Deadline 9 Oct 2026 → PRF Committee meets May 2027 (**~7 months**) → ACS Board approval ~June 2027 (**~8 months**) → earliest award start 1 July 2027 (**~8.7 months**).

Worked example for the next cycle:
- Deadline 12 Mar 2027 → PRF Committee meets October 2027 (**~7 months**) → earliest award start 1 Jan 2028 (**~9.6 months**).

Practical consequence for an ECR on a tenure clock: from the day you start writing to the day you can spend a dollar is roughly a year. If you are within the DNI 3-year or UNI 5-year eligibility window, count backwards from the SUBMISSION deadline, not the award date — eligibility is judged at application.

The precise date applicants are notified of the outcome is not published anywhere I could find; see unresolved.

review_stages.stage: Administrative + scope compliance check by PRF program staff. Every proposal is screened for four things (funder's wording): "Completeness and correctness of the application; Fundamental nature of the research topic; Relevance to petroleum or fossil fuels; and Extent to which the proposed research differs from prior graduate and postdoctoral research" (DNI) / "is a new direction for the principal investigator" (ND) / "Description of the impact on advanced scientific education of students" (UR). THIS IS THE REAL FILTER. Proposals that fail are "denied without external review, or may be rejected by the PRF Committee." For UR and UNI the funder adds that "poorly crafted proposals that are deemed to be 'noncompetitive' will be denied without external review." Proposals over 4,000 words "will not be considered."
review_stages.timing: At / shortly after the deadline. Exact turnaround not published.

review_stages.stage: External peer review. You must supply at least SIX suggested reviewers (name, institution, email) in the portal, plus an optional 150-character "Why are you choosing this reviewer?" note, and you may list reviewers to exclude. Conflict rules are strict: no former mentors, students, collaborators or co-authors within the past 48 months, no colleagues at your current or former institutions, no family, no financial relationships — and "a PI may not suggest a reviewer whom the PI has suggested to PRF in the last 4 years."
review_stages.timing: Between the deadline and the Committee meeting — i.e. inside the ~7-month gap. PRF does not publish how long external review itself takes.

review_stages.stage: PRF Science Panels. Discipline panels (the Annual Report indexes reports as DNI1–10, ND1–10, UNI1–10, UR1–10, implying ten panels per mechanism). You choose your panel yourself in the application: "PRF Panel Selection – Select the PRF Panel that best reflects your proposal." Panel members see your resubmission statement — the funder notes the statement of changes "is just for the use of the Program Manager and the PRF Science Panel members."
review_stages.timing: Between external review and the Committee meeting. Not separately dated.

review_stages.stage: ACS PRF Committee meeting — the funding decision. The Committee "makes relative rankings of proposals and recommendations for funding." Criteria are published and are weighted DIFFERENTLY by mechanism: for ND, "Newness of the proposed research for the lead PI" is criterion #1; for DNI and UR, overall scientific merit is #1 and newness is #3; for DNI, student-education impact is #2.
review_stages.timing: May (for Sept–Oct submissions) or October (for Feb–Mar submissions) — ~7 months after the deadline. Next: May 2027 for the 9 Oct 2026 deadline.

review_stages.stage: ACS Board of Directors approval. The Committee recommends; the ACS Board approves. Evidence: C&EN headline "ACS Board approves 113 new PRF projects" published June 2026, following the May 2026 Committee meeting; the spring 2026 round totalled $12,295,000. VIA SEARCH INDEX ONLY — cen.acs.org returns HTTP 406 to both plain fetch and a rendering browser, so I could not read the article text itself.
review_stages.timing: ~1 month after the Committee meeting (May meeting → June Board item). Medium confidence.

review_stages.stage: Notification to applicants of the outcome.
review_stages.timing: NOT FOUND. PRF publishes no notification date or turnaround. Logically bounded between the Committee meeting and the earliest start date (i.e. between May and 1 July, or between October and 1 January), but I could not source this.

review_stages.stage: Earliest award start. Fixed by rule, not negotiable upward: 1 July after a May Committee meeting; 1 January after an October Committee meeting. Start date must be the first of a month and the budget period must end 31 August.
review_stages.timing: ~9 months after the deadline (1 July 2027 for the 9 Oct 2026 deadline).

result.resubmission_policy:
**Allowed, but hard-capped, and there is a forced waiting cycle for ND and UR.**

**The cap (verbatim, ACS PRF Grant Application Components, Fall 2026 PDF):** "Resubmission Justification / Statement of Modifications – If the research topic was previously denied by the PRF Committee, a statement describing what has been changed in the revised version is required. [Note: Applicants are limited to an initial application and a maximum of two resubmissions on the same topic.]"

So: 1 original + 2 resubmissions = 3 bites at one topic, then that topic is done.

**Is an "introduction page" required?** No — PRF does NOT use an NIH-style Introduction page inside the proposal PDF. The statement of changes is a **web-form field in the portal**, and the funder is explicit that it must be kept OUT of the document: "If this is a resubmission of a previously denied proposal, you will need to answer the question, 'What has been changed in this revised version?' in the online submission form. This information is just for the use of the Program Manager and the PRF Science Panel members, so it is not to be included in the proposal document" (ND Application Instructions, Rev 02/2024). Putting it in the PDF would also eat your 4,000 words.

**Fresh reviewers — a trap that catches people.** "'Revised and resubmitted' proposals are sent to a different set of reviewers than those asked to evaluate the initial proposal." And correspondingly, in the suggested-reviewer section: "Resubmissions: If the proposal is a resubmission, reviewers listed on a prior submission may not be included." So you must have a second slate of six clean, conflict-free names ready.

**Time window / forced skip — differs by mechanism:**
- **ND:** "Principal investigators (lead PI or co-PI) may have only one ND grant application considered in a 12-month period. Thus, a principal investigator (lead PI or co-PI) who has an ND proposal denied may not submit another ND proposal until the PRF Committee meeting one year later." I.e. you skip a cycle — denied at the May meeting, your next ND attempt is the following May, not the intervening October.
- **UR:** same one-year rule — a PI with a UR proposal denied may not submit another UR proposal until the PRF Committee meeting one year later (via search index; the UR page on acs.org currently returns a genuine ACS 403, and PRF's own knowledge base copy at prfgrant.acs.org/pkb/s/article/Undergraduate-Research-UR-Grants was truncated before the Limitations block).
- **DNI:** "New investigators may have only three (3) DNI grant applications considered and/or one (1) DNI grant funded in their career. Thereafter, the new investigator may apply to the New Directions (ND) Grant Program." One proposal per meeting.
- **UNI:** identical structure — "only three (3) UNI grant applications considered and/or one (1) UNI grant funded in their career. Thereafter, the new investigator may apply to the Undergraduate Research (UR) program."

**Overriding limit regardless of resubmission status:** one proposal per meeting; you may not hold more than one active PRF grant at a time; and "A principal investigator with an active PRF research grant, including a grant on time extension, may not submit an application for a new grant."

**What must actually change.** The funder's own checklist names failure to revise as a top rejection reason: "No outline of revisions. For a previously denied proposal, which has been revised and resubmitted, the PI did not address reviewers' concerns/comments and did not include, with the application, a summary of major changes." Note the tension with the instruction above — address reviewer comments substantively in the science, and put the summary of changes in the portal field.
result.page_limits:
**There is no page limit. PRF works in WORD counts — this is the single most common formatting misunderstanding for people arriving from NIH/NSF.**

Technical proposal (single PDF, uploaded), verbatim from the Fall 2026 Application Components PDF:
- "The technical proposal must include the title, abstract, scientific narrative, references, and any figures and tables in a single PDF."
- "The document should be double-spaced in 12-point font with 1-inch margins." (ND instructions name the permitted faces: "12-point font (Times Roman, Arial, or Courier)".)
- "The narrative is limited to a maximum of 4,000 words. The title, abstract, references, figure captions, and table captions do not count toward the word limit."
- "Include the word count at the end of the narrative."
- "References must be included in the same PDF; do not submit them separately."
- "Reference formatting: List all authors for every cited work and include the complete article title. Truncated author lists or shortened titles are not acceptable." (The checklist adds: "Do not use 'et al.' in reference citations.")
- Number pages in the footer. No institutional cover letter is required; if included, place it after the references.
- Enforcement is absolute: "Submissions that exceed the 4,000 word limit for the technical proposal will not be considered."

Word-limited fields entered in the portal (not in the PDF):
- Abstract — **250 words max** (and it must ALSO appear at the start of the uploaded technical proposal PDF)
- Petroleum Relevance Statement — **100 words max**
- New Research Direction Statement — **500 words max**
- Scientific Education Impact and Mentoring Statement — **500 words max**
- Available Facilities and Instrumentation — **500 words max**
- Suggested-reviewer justification — 150 characters (optional)
- Keywords — up to 5 (optional)

**Variation by mechanism (from the same PDF):**
- Publications/presentations depth: "For ND and UR grants, publications during the past five years are required. For DNI and UNI grants, complete publication lists are required." Same split for presentations.
- Teaching Information block — **UR and UNI only** (teaching duties; % time on research in academic year; % time on research in summer; number of undergraduates who did research with the PI in the past 12 months).
- Co-PI permitted — **ND and UR only** (one co-PI). Not DNI or UNI.
- Postdoctoral Fellow Salary Support budget line — **ND and DNI only**.
- Student-support floor: **≥60%** of budget for ND and DNI; **≥40%** for UR. UR additionally may not pay tuition, postdocs, or doctoral students, and may support M.S. students only if undergraduates are also supported.
- Budget total is FIXED per mechanism and mismatching it is a listed failure: "Budget for the wrong amount (must be $125,000)" for ND. ND $125,000 / DNI $110,000 / UR $70,000 / UNI $55,000.
- New-direction framing differs: "For ND and UR grant types, the PI should not have publications in the area they justify as a new direction. For DNI and UNI grant types, the project must be distinct from the PI's graduate or postdoctoral research."

**DRIFT WARNING — the funder's own pages disagree with each other.** The proposal-submission web page (acs.org/.../salesforce-proposal-submission-help.html) still says the ND/UR new-direction statement and the UNI/UR mentoring statement must be "no longer than 1 page." The Fall 2026 Application Components PDF, which is the current cycle's document, replaces both with 500-word portal fields. Use the PDF. Likewise the older ND Application Instructions PDF is Rev 02/2024 and predates the AI-disclosure and UN-SDG fields.
required_documents: UPLOADED FILES (only two, plus optional letters) — 1) Technical Proposal: ONE PDF containing title, 250-word abstract, scientific narrative (≤4,000 words), references cited, figures and tables, with the word count typed at the end and pages numbered in the footer. 2) Signed Signature Sheet: generated by the portal ('Download for Signatures'), signed by the PI, the co-PI if any, AND an authorised institutional official — 'The institutional official is the person who is authorized to commit the PI's institution to performing the proposed research, and is not the Department Chair. All signatures are required on both pages' (title page and budget page; each signatory signs in two places). Uploaded back as a PDF under file type 'Signature Sheet'.

PORTAL WEB-FORM CONTENT — Principal Investigator contact information (name, institution, department, address, ORCID); Grants Office information (general grants office email, Grant Officer name and contact details) and Institutional Endorsing Official; Co-PI details (ND and UR only); Institutional Reference Number (enter 'NA' if none).

Applicant background block: highest degree offered in the PI's department; PI appointment type (tenured/tenure-track or not); DATE OF FIRST FACULTY APPOINTMENT (this is what the DNI 3-year / UNI 5-year clocks are checked against); academic training in reverse chronological order including Ph.D. thesis title and supervisor and all postdoctoral appointments and supervisors; professional experience; significant honors and awards.

Current and Pending Research Support — for PI and Co-PI: all current grants (title, amount, source, period, and relationship to this proposal); all pending applications (title, amount requested, source, relationship); and 'Describe any active start-up support from your institution.' Enter 'None' where applicable. Note PRF checks this for overlap: 'PRF will not support a project having overlap, or partial overlap, with research funded by another agency,' and you must keep the PRF office advised of the status of applications elsewhere while yours is under consideration.
Publications and Presentations — ND/UR: past five years. DNI/UNI: complete lists. Include article titles and all co-authors.

Teaching Information — UR and UNI ONLY: teaching duties; % time devoted to research in the academic year; % time devoted to research in summer; number of undergraduates who did research with the PI in the past 12 months. (UNI additionally requires a summary of the highest academic degree awarded in the PI's department and available facilities.)

Scientific statements entered in the portal: Proposal Title; Abstract (≤250 words); PRF Panel Selection; Petroleum Relevance Statement (≤100 words — 'Describe how the proposed work advances fundamental research in the petroleum field'); New Research Direction Statement (≤500 words); Scientific Education Impact and Mentoring Statement (≤500 words); Available Facilities and Instrumentation (≤500 words); Safety Statement (describe significant risks/hazards and mitigation — a missing safety statement is a listed rejection reason; guidance at www.acs.org/safety).
Resubmission Justification / Statement of Modifications — REQUIRED if the topic was previously denied. Entered in the web form, explicitly NOT in the proposal PDF.

Suggested Reviewers — minimum SIX, with name, institution and email, plus optional 150-character rationale. Plus an optional 'Reviewers to Exclude' list. Strict COI rules: no collaborators/co-authors within 48 months, no former advisors or advisees, no colleagues at your institution, no family, no financial relationships; and no reviewer you suggested to PRF in the last 4 years; and for a resubmission, none of the reviewers named on the prior submission.

Budget — project start and end dates plus per-year values in fixed categories: PI Support (≤$8,000/grant year, fringe included; ND/DNI cap $16,000 total, UR cap $24,000 total; not available to PIs outside the US); Graduate Student Support; Undergraduate Student Support; Postdoctoral Fellow Salary (ND and DNI only); Tuition; Expendable Supplies & Services; Capital Equipment (≤$5,000 over the project, and 'discouraged'); Conference Travel (≤$2,000/grant year); Publication Fees (≤$2,000 over the project, may cover open-access fees, language editing, covers); Field Work (PI) and Field Work (Students). Plus a Budget Justification Narrative. No overhead/indirect, no secretarial or administrative salaries, no technicians, contractors, consultants or visiting faculty. Total must equal the mechanism's fixed amount exactly.
Demographic information for PI and Co-PI, including ORCID.

Similarity Check Acknowledgement — 'The applicant acknowledges that this application may be subject to a similarity/plagiarism check.' PRF states it 'reserves the right to scan proposals for plagiarism.'

Description of AI Tools Used — 'If applicants disclose use of AI tools in preparing their application, a description of how AI tools were used is required.' (New in the Fall 2026 components document.)

OPTIONAL: Keywords (up to 5); UN SDG Alignment; Collaborations — identify collaborators and the nature of the collaboration, note any who are current ACS PRF grantees or applicants, and upload a letter from each collaborator in the 'All Other Documents' section.

CONDITIONAL LETTERS: (a) If you are NOT tenure-track — a brief statement describing your appointment PLUS a Department Chair's letter affirming you meet all three PRF eligibility criteria. (b) If you are claiming a DNI/UNI eligibility extension for a tenure-clock extension (parental leave, medical leave, other career-interrupting circumstances formally recognised by your institution) — a confirmation letter from institutional leadership specifying the duration; PRF publishes a template at acs.org/content/dam/acsorg/funding/grants/prf/prf-exception-template-jan2026.pdf. The PRF extension matches the institution's.
result.program_officer_norms:
**EXPECTED AND ACTIVELY INVITED — this is an NIH-style funder on this axis, not a keep-your-distance foundation.** PRF names its Program Managers/Officers with their disciplines and direct emails on every programme page, publishes a phone number for the Research Grants Office, and has produced a video literally titled "The PRF Program Manager as a Resource" (vimeo.com/172902103, linked from the For Applicants page).

The funder solicits contact in its own words, repeatedly:
- On scope: "The PRF Committee routinely evaluates the research areas supported by PRF. For more details, we encourage you to reach out to a PRF program officer or PRFsupport@acs.org."
- On whether your idea counts as a new direction: "We suggest calling the ACS Research Grants Office at 202-872-4481 to discuss the suitability of your project with a Program Manager if you are in doubt."
- On eligibility: "Please call the ACS Research Grants Office at 202-872-4481 to discuss your eligibility with a Program Manager if you have questions." And for tenure-clock exceptions: "If you have any questions, contact your program officer."
- On budget: "If you have any questions about allowable budget allocations, please contact the appropriate Program Manager before submitting a proposal."
- And the checklist of common errors opens: "If in doubt, please call ACS PRF (202-872-4481) or email the appropriate Program Manager well before the submission deadline."

**WHEN in the cycle.** Well before the deadline — the funder's phrase is "well before the submission deadline" and "before submitting a proposal." In practice that means during the writing phase, i.e. weeks to a couple of months ahead, not in the final days (when staff are absorbed by submissions and nothing can be changed after the bell anyway). There is no pre-proposal, LOI or concept-paper stage, so the phone call IS the pre-submission triage.

**Program Officers by discipline (current as of Sept 2026, from the ND/DNI/UNI programme pages):**
- Dr. William Aumiller — Organic Structures, Dynamics, and Mechanisms; Chemical Physics/Physical Chemistry — w_aumiller@acs.org
- Dr. Thomas Clancy — Polymer Science, Engineering, Chemistry, and Petroleum Engineering — t_clancy@acs.org
- Dr. Laura Fernandez — Surface Science and Materials Science — l_fernandez@acs.org
- Dr. Allegra Liberman-Martin — Synthetic Organic Chemistry and Inorganic Chemistry — a_liberman@acs.org
- Dr. Johan Schijf — Geochemistry and Biogeochemical Cycling; Geology and Geophysics — J_Schijf@acs.org
Office: The Petroleum Research Fund, ACS, 1155 16th Street NW, Washington DC 20036. Phone (202) 872-4481. General: PRFsupport@acs.org. (Portal/technical problems go to prfsupport@acs.org, not to a PO.)

**What experienced applicants actually ask.** INFERENCE — PRF publishes no survey of enquiries; this is derived from the specific questions the funder itself routes to a Program Manager, and from which failure modes it lists as fatal:
1. "Is my topic in scope?" — is this fundamental rather than applied, and is it in the "petroleum field"? Topic outside scope is failure reason #1 on the funder's checklist, and staff can kill it before you write.
2. "Is this enough of a new direction?" — the highest-value question, because a proposal judged not-a-new-direction is "denied without external review" and never reaches a reviewer. The FAQ gives worked acceptable/unacceptable examples (e.g. a computational chemist moving from Diels-Alder to Cope rearrangement is NOT new; applying the same computational expertise to oil/mineral interactions IS).
3. "Am I eligible?" — non-tenure-track appointments, community-college faculty, emeritus faculty supervising postdocs, tenure-clock extensions, eligible countries for ND/UR.
4. "Does my budget work?" — the 60%/40% student-support floors, the $8,000 PI stipend cap, capital equipment, what counts as field work vs conference travel.
5. "Which PRF Panel should I select?" — since the applicant chooses the panel, and the panel determines who judges it.

Note for international applicants: ND and UR are open to PIs in 50+ countries, with the eligible list re-derived annually from the top third of Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index, plus US sanctions screening of applicants, institutions and funding sources. DNI and UNI are US-only. A PO call is the sensible way to confirm your country is on the current list.
result.funded_examples_source:
**There is NO NIH-RePORTER equivalent and PRF does not publish sample funded applications or reviewer summary statements.** What exists instead is the ACS PRF **Annual Report on Research**, which publishes the grantees' own narrative progress reports — searchable by title, institution, PI, and by grant type/panel.

**1. ACS PRF Annual Report site — https://acswebcontent.acs.org/prfar/<year>/** (2016 = the 61st Annual Report; confirmed reachable). Structure:
- "Grants Awarded" (media/grants.html) — round summary plus "Download a list of ACS PRF grants awarded in [year]" as a PDF, and per-mechanism counts and amounts.
- Reports browsable "By Title" (REPORT.html), "By Institution" (affiliationa.html), "By Principal Investigator" (authora.html), and via a Table of Contents (media/TOC.html) organised by grant type and panel — DNI1–10, ND1–10, UNI1–10, UR1–10, plus SE.
- Individual report pages carry grant number, grant type, PI, institution, title and the full narrative. Verified example: https://acswebcontent.acs.org/prfar/2016/Paper13837.html — grant **54824-DNI1**, Jennifer L. Roizen (Duke University), "Site- and Enantioselective Electrophilic Halogen-Transfer Processes," opening: "Two powerful approaches promise to transform strategic small molecule assembly: late-stage atom-transfer processes and cross-coupling reactions."
- Also "Researcher Stories" (media/stories.html) and "Featured Reports" (media/features.html) — short profiles of funded projects.
- Full-report PDF, e.g. media/ACS_PRF_61st.pdf.

**Use it this way:** find three funded grants of YOUR mechanism in YOUR panel, at institutions like yours, and read them for calibration on what PRF's scope filter actually lets through and what "new direction" looks like in practice. Grant numbers encode the type (e.g. 54824-**DNI1** = DNI, panel 1), so the numbering itself tells you which panel judged the work.

**CAVEAT, flagged honestly:** these are progress reports on funded work, NOT the applications. And availability is patchy — only the 2016 year responded; 2018, 2019, 2021 and 2023 returned 403, and acs.org's own annual-report.html index page currently returns a genuine ACS 403 ("This page is forbidden"). I could not establish whether recent years are still published or where their index lives. See unresolved.

**2. C&EN round announcements** — C&EN publishes each funding round, e.g. "ACS Board approves 113 new PRF projects" (June 2026) and "Petroleum Research Fund grant submissions open for 2026" (Jan 2026); the spring 2026 round totalled $12,295,000. VIA SEARCH INDEX ONLY — cen.acs.org returned HTTP 406 to both plain fetch and a rendering browser, so I could not read the articles.

**3. JACS 65th-anniversary open-access virtual issue** — a retrospective of JACS papers by chemists who held PRF funding, linked from the PRF homepage. Useful for seeing what PRF seed money grew into, not for application craft.

**4. The funder's own craft materials** (better value than hunting for sample applications, and the closest thing PRF offers to a worked example):
- "What makes a competitive proposal?" — vimeo.com/41306667
- "What Makes a Proposal a New Direction?" — vimeo.com/132978944
- "The PRF Program Manager as a Resource" — vimeo.com/172902103
- "What makes a good ACS PRF grant proposal reviewer?" — vimeo.com/64588132
- The 14-item "Checklist of Common Errors" (reproduced in full in the ND Application Instructions PDF) — this is effectively PRF telling you its rejection reasons in rank order.
- The FAQ's acceptable/not-acceptable New Directions worked examples.
- An "Eligibility Self-check" tool and a "PRF quiz" on the PRF homepage.

**5. Your own institution** — since every PRF proposal needs an institutional endorsing official's signature, your research office has copies of prior submissions from your campus. That is the most realistic route to reading a real PRF application.

result.funder_system: American Council of Learned Societies (ACLS) — a private federation of scholarly societies, not a federal agency. It runs ~20 named competitions per cycle in the humanities and interpretive social sciences, some wholly ACLS-funded (ACLS Fellowships, HBCU Faculty Fellowships/Grants, Digital Justice Grants, Leading Edge) and many co-branded with a partner funder that supplies the money while ACLS runs the machinery (Mellon/ACLS, Luce/ACLS, Robert H. N. Ho Family Foundation, NYPL Cullman Center). The machinery below — one portal, one account, fixed annual deadlines, two-to-three stage peer review, reviewer feedback on request — is common across all of them. What varies by mechanism is page limits, whether reference letters are accepted at all, and how many times you may reapply. Scale: "In the 2024-25 competition year, ACLS awarded approximately $21 million to nearly 400 scholars." Selectivity where published: the 2026 Mellon/ACLS Dissertation Innovation cohort of "50 fellows was selected from a pool of over 1,000 applicants" (~5%). ACLS Fellowships recently awarded "approximately $3.5 million to 63 exceptional scholars"; at least 60 are promised for 2026-27, but ACLS does not publish that competition's applicant pool.
result.deadline_structure:

Nearly every deadline is 5:00 PM ET; the one exception in the current cycle is the Graves Awards nomination at 9:00 PM ET.

result.funded_examples_source:
Three distinct resources, of unequal value. Ranked by what actually helps a first-time applicant:

1. BEST — ACLS PUBLISHES COMPLETE SAMPLE APPLICATION PACKETS (PDF), for the Mellon/ACLS Dissertation Innovation Fellowship:
   - https://www.acls.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/DIF-Sample-Application.pdf (48 pages; confirmed HTTP 200 and text-extracted 2026-09-18)
   - https://www.acls.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/DIF-2223-Sample-Application.pdf (confirmed HTTP 200)
   IMPORTANT CAVEAT, since the filename misleads: these are NOT funded proposals. They are a screen-by-screen print-out of the entire live OFA application system — Description, Eligibility, Evaluation Criteria, Instructions, program FAQ, technical FAQ, every field of the application form (contact, demographics, education, awards, publications, dissertation project, administrative info), the Reference Letters page, Proposal Upload, and Submit. Their value is that you can read every question and every character limit before you create an account. Nothing else ACLS publishes shows you the form in advance. Do not cite them as examples of winning prose.

2. FELLOWS AND GRANTEES DATABASE — https://www.acls.org/fellows-grantees/. "More than 12,000 scholars" with records running from at least 1943 to 2026, filterable by Fellowship Year and by Related Program. Shows name, award year, affiliation and PROJECT TITLE only. Example entry: "Bea Abbott, 2026, University of Kentucky, 'Visualizing Border Space from Below: Networked Images and Contested Visual Politics in the Aegean Sea'." NO abstracts. Its real use is calibration: filter to your program and year, read 40 titles, and you learn the register, scale and ambition ACLS actually funds in your field — and you find the named people in your subfield to email.
   Companion hubs: https://www.acls.org/recent-fellows/ and https://www.acls.org/recent-awardees/ (a navigation hub to 23 per-program awardee lists).

3. AWARD ANNOUNCEMENT NEWS POSTS — e.g. https://www.acls.org/news/acls-awards-2026-mellon-acls-dissertation-innovation-fellowships/. These carry short prose descriptions of several fellows' projects (a paragraph, not an abstract) plus the selectivity figures ACLS chooses to disclose.

NOT AVAILABLE, and worth saying plainly: there is no ACLS equivalent of NIH RePORTER. There are no published summary statements, no searchable abstract corpus, and no sample application packet for ACLS Fellowships itself (only for Mellon/ACLS DIF). The nearest substitute for a summary statement is the reviewer feedback ACLS will send YOU on request after you are declined (see review_stages).
