result.funder_system:
Cystic Fibrosis Foundation (CFF) — a single-disease private advocacy funder, EIN 13-1930701, Bethesda MD. Runs its own end-to-end grants operation: its own portal, its own standing review committees, its own RFAs. NOT a federal system — no Grants.gov, no eRA Commons, no SF424, no percentile/payline, no study-section roster, no public award database. $215.5M spent on research and development in 2025 (cff.org/research-clinical-trials/research-we-fund).

The whole academic portfolio (~25 mechanisms) runs on ONE set of machinery, which is why it is worth learning once. Three archetypes differ only in cadence and whether an LOI gates entry: (A) single-stage basic-science and training awards (Research Grant, Pilot & Feasibility, Postdoctoral Fellowship, all Path-to-a-Cure variants) — May and December cycles; (B) single-stage career-development awards (Harry Shwachman, LeRoy Matthews, Clinical Fellowship) — one February cycle; (C) two-stage invite-only clinical awards (Clinical Research Award, Clinical Pilot & Feasibility) — mandatory LOI, then invited full application.

Standing review committees (cff.org/researchers/how-we-fund-research): Research and Research Training (RRT) and Path to a Cure (PTAC) for basic/translational; Clinical Research Committee (CRC) for clinical; Physician-Scientist Training Programs (PTP) for fellowships and physician-scientist career awards. Ad hoc committees for targeted RFAs. For some clinical programs, "people with CF and their families also review the applications and provide feedback."

Administrative home: Grants and Contracts Management and Administration (GCMA) Office, 4550 Montgomery Ave., Suite 1100 N, Bethesda, MD 20814; grants@cff.org; 301-841-2614 / 301-841-2671; 800-FIGHT-CF.

Base rates: published only for the Clinical Research Award — "On average, the Foundation invites about 35% of the investigators to submit full applications and funds roughly 20% of full applications" (2027 CRA Policies and Guidelines, Section II). No published success rate for Research Grant, P&F or training awards.
result.submission_portal:
awards.cff.org — CFF's own Grants Management System (Altum-style). Not proposalCentral, not Grants.gov, not NSPIRES. Every academic mechanism, including the CFF/NIH R01-Unfunded bridge award, submits here. Deadline is 5:00 p.m. ET on the stated date. "The CF Foundation reviews applications electronically, and only documents submitted online at http://awards.cff.org will be reviewed" (Research Grant P&G, Section VIII).

FIVE HIDDEN LONG-LEAD ITEMS — this is the part first-timers miss:

1. ACCOUNT + PROFILE, 2 WEEKS AHEAD. "We strongly encourage all applicants to pre-register their profile, institution, contacts, and Title of their application at least two weeks prior to the application deadline. This will help to ensure the CF Foundation Grants & Contracts Management and Administration (GCMA) Office is able to assist all applicants with potential system-related queries prior to the Application Deadline." First-timers must create a username/password and complete a profile before starting an application. Register under "Domestic Institution" or "International Institution" — picking wrong misroutes the whole application.

2. THE AIO STEP — YOUR CLICK IS NOT SUBMISSION. The PI clicks "Submit to Authorized Institution Official for Acceptance"; status becomes "Pending Authorized Institution Official Acceptance" and the application LOCKS. Your institution's Authorized Institution Official must then open it via My Applications > Pending Authorized Institution Official Acceptance, enter AIO initials on the ASSURANCE STATEMENT(S) tab, and click "Submit to CFF." Your sponsored-programs office needs an awards.cff.org account and must act before 5 p.m. ET. (A "Revise AIO" button reverts it to Draft if changes are needed.)

3. INSTITUTION RECORD BY EIN/TIN. Domestic applicants verify the institution by entering EIN/TIN; if not found you must add the legal entity. GCMA will not issue an Award Letter without the institution's W-9 and 501(c)(3) letter on file. Non-US: W-8BEN-E is required, plus a tax equivalency letter or a letter stating none is available, plus a CFF International Institution Form (USA Patriot Act / Treasury anti-terrorist-financing compliance).

4. REFEREE LETTERS GO IN BEFORE YOU SUBMIT. Junior investigators invite referees through the REFERENCES tab; referees Accept/Decline by email. "The applicant should inform Referees to submit the letters at least one (1) week prior to the application deadline... Once the application has been submitted, no documents can be added." Letters must not be password-protected or encrypted (breaks PDF assembly). The applicant cannot see the letters.

5. UPSTREAM GATES FOR CLINICAL WORK. CRA/CP&FA: the LOI must be submitted AND approved ~4.5 months before the full application. CFF Biorepository specimen requests must be finalized "no later than six weeks before the full application deadline. Late requests may not be processed in time for CRC review."

Mechanics: uploads are compiled by the system into one PDF — preview via "Application Full Print." Save at the bottom of every page; return to drafts via "My Applications" > "Draft Applications", NOT via "Funding Opportunities". Formatting is fixed across mechanisms: Times New Roman 12 or Arial 11, margins no less than half an inch each side.

Note on a stale third-party claim: a Weill Cornell research-office page says the CFF/NIH-unfunded award goes through proposalCENTRAL. CFF's own page says awards.cff.org. Trust CFF; the Cornell page is dated 2018.

result.resubmission_policy:
ALLOWED, BUT HARD-CAPPED AT TWO CYCLES, AND THE REQUIRED PAPERWORK IS UNLIKE NIH'S.

How many:
- Research Grant and Pilot & Feasibility (verbatim, Section VII): "Applications that have not been funded in two review cycles will not be accepted for further consideration by CF Foundation. (Exceptions for one additional resubmission may be considered for tenure-track PIs who are pre-tenure with prior approval from the Program Officer.)" In practice: original + one resubmission. A third attempt exists only if you are pre-tenure on the tenure track AND you cleared it with the Program Officer in advance.
- Clinical Research Award (verbatim): "Applications that have not been discussed in two review meetings will not be accepted for further consideration by the CF Foundation. Applicants must address reviewer critiques in order to resubmit their applications during future application cycles." Note the wording is "discussed", so a triaged application that was never discussed may not burn a cycle — worth asking the PO.
- Harry Shwachman / career awards: no numeric cap stated in the RFA; the only stated condition is "Applicants must address reviewer critiques in order to resubmit their applications during future application cycles."

What must change — three things, all mandatory:
1. Flag it. "In order to resubmit unfunded applications during future application cycles, applicants must indicate that the application is a resubmission."
2. Upload a CRITIQUE RESPONSE (a downloadable template inside awards.cff.org). Verbatim: "If the application is a resubmission of a previously declined application, please provide a point-by-point response to the prior reviews. There is no page limit to your responses, but please be concise and succinct." This is CFF's answer to NIH's Introduction page — but it is a SEPARATE UPLOAD, not part of the research plan, and it is UNLIMITED in length, not one page. There is no NIH-style "Introduction to Resubmission" page.
3. Revise the science AND mark the changes. Verbatim: "If the application is a resubmission of an earlier one, revisions must be clearly indicated by a change in font, bolded or underlined. The CF Foundation will not review resubmissions that have not been revised." And: "In addition to providing the response to critiques, the research plan must also be revised and clearly marked to show changes from the previous submission. Research plans that are not clearly revised may not be reviewed." A cosmetic resubmission is rejected without review.

Separate LOI resubmission path (clinical track): "Applicants whose LOI was not approved in an earlier submission may resubmit the LOI with (1) appropriate revisions, and (2) an attachment that provides a point-by-point response to the limitations noted by the reviewers." That attachment has its own cap: "Maximum of three (3) pages."

Time window: no calendar expiry is stated anywhere in the RFAs. The real constraints are (a) the two-cycle count, and (b) the throughput caps — one Research Grant application per calendar year, one application per laboratory per cycle (resubmission vs original counts the same), one research grant + one P&F per 12 months. So a resubmission normally lands 6 or 12 months after the original, and choosing to resubmit means giving up the lab's other shot that cycle.

Ceiling that can block you regardless: "Multiple CF Foundation Research Grants held by a single investigator will not be permitted... when the total combined funding exceeds $168,000 per year. In such cases, the most recent application submitted will be considered administratively ineligible." And PIs above $200,000/yr in combined CFF direct costs (with an end date more than 6 months out) need Program Officer approval before applying at all.
result.page_limits:
FORMAT IS IDENTICAL ACROSS MECHANISMS: Times New Roman 12 or Arial 11; margins no less than half an inch each side; single-sided; PI name in the header; page numbers tracked by the provided template. Literature Cited is EXCLUDED from the research plan limit in every mechanism.

RESEARCH PLAN page limit — this is the one thing that varies by mechanism (all verified in each mechanism's own Policies & Guidelines PDF):
- Pilot and Feasibility Award: SIX (6) pages
- Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Award: SEVEN (7) pages
- Postdoc-to-Faculty Transition Award: SEVEN (7) pages
- Harry Shwachman Clinical Investigator Award: TEN (10) pages
- Research Grant: TWELVE (12) pages
- Clinical Research Award: THIRTEEN (13) pages, of which "One page is to be dedicated to the Aims of the proposal"

Enforcement is absolute and identical in every RFA: "Applications exceeding this page limit will not be reviewed."

INSIDE the research plan:
- "Hypothesis and Specific Aims... Do not exceed one page."
- Required subsections (basic science): Hypothesis and Specific Aims; Background and Science/Significance; Preliminary Results; Experimental Design and Methods; Limitations and Potential Pitfalls; Consultant Arrangements; Literature Cited. CRA adds an Innovation Statement.
- FIGURES MUST BE IN THE RESEARCH PLAN, at minimum 11 pt: "Key figures and legends must be included in the Research Plan and should be of sufficient quality and size (at least 11 pt font) to be evaluated by the reviewer. If uploaded as Appendices, they will NOT be reviewed." You cannot buy space by exiling figures to an appendix.

OTHER LIMITS:
- Biographical Sketch (NIH format): "Do not exceed five (5) pages per person." International applicants may use an equivalent format.
- Other Support: no page limit.
- Facilities Available: no page limit ("Use continuation pages, if necessary").
- Critique Response (resubmission): no page limit.
- Response to Prior LOI Critique (CRA only): maximum three (3) pages.
- CHARACTER limits, entered directly in the portal, not uploaded: Lay Abstract, Scientific Abstract, and "Project Alignment to Research Priorities and Expected Outcomes" each "no more than 2,000 characters (including spaces)"; "Summary of Relevance to CF Foundation mission" "no more than 3,000 characters (including spaces)". The Project Alignment abstract is NEW in the current RFAs and must "Identify up to three specific outcomes anticipated upon completion of the project."
- Appendices are restricted by category, not page count: assurance certifications (IRB/IACUC/IBC), signed Letters of Support, signed Letters of Collaboration from Co-PIs. CRA additionally allows "Up to three (3) reprints of the applicant's work relating to the general area of research in the proposal."
required_documents: Research Plan (upload; template provided in awards.cff.org) — page limit varies by mechanism, 6 to 13 pages, figures must be embedded

Budget Detail — entered in-system via 'Edit Budget', per year and per subcontract. Salary capped at the federal salary cap ($228,000 FY2026); travel capped at $1,500/person/yr; tuition capped at $10,000/person/yr; indirect costs up to 12% (0% on major equipment, software, software licenses and tuition); indirect on only the first $25,000 of each subcontract
Budget Justification (upload; template) — provided individually for each year of support requested, single or separate PDFs
Biographical Sketches of Key Personnel, NIH format (upload; template) — PI first, max 5 pages each; dependent faculty must also supply the lab PI's biosketch
Other Support, for all key personnel (upload; template) — no page limit; used to detect scientific and budgetary overlap; >100% effort not permitted
Facilities Available (upload; template) — no page limit

Results of Past and Current CFF/CFFT Support (upload; template) — past 5 years, each entry must give CFF/CFFT Award #, PI, project title, applicant's title on the project, start/end dates, total award amount, and results. Training awards require the MENTOR's version of this form

Abstracts entered online: Lay Abstract (<=2,000 char), Scientific Abstract (<=2,000 char), Project Alignment to Research Priorities and Expected Outcomes (<=2,000 char, name up to three anticipated outcomes), Summary of Relevance to the CF Foundation Mission (<=3,000 char)

Organizational Assurances declared on the GENERAL tab — IRB, IACUC, and/or IBC/rDNA approval status at time of submission; approval letters uploaded as appendices when available. CFF will not release payment to the institution until these are on file with GCMA

Institutional tax documentation — US: current W-9 and 501(c)(3) letter (no Award Letter issues without them); for-profit: W-9 plus IRS documentation of federal tax status; non-US: W-8BEN-E (required) plus a tax equivalency letter or a letter stating none is available, plus the CFF International Institution Form

Letters of Reference — JUNIOR INVESTIGATORS ONLY (defined as: no prior CFF Research Grant or NIH equivalent such as R01/R21/R23 as PI, AND within the first five years of a first appointment at Assistant Professor level or equivalent). Required from the Department Chair (must confirm release of space/facilities and guarantee the investigator's time commitment; for a current fellow, confirm the pending faculty appointment) plus at least two others familiar with the applicant's scientific interests and abilities. Referees are invited through the REFERENCES tab and must upload BEFORE the applicant submits; not visible to the applicant; must not be password-protected

Letter(s) of Support — for investigators NEW TO CF (defined as: has not previously published in CF, and has not received extramural funding for a CF-focused project). Must come from an established CF investigator/clinician collaborator and explicitly state how the work is relevant to CF and what the collaborator will provide (expertise, CF-relevant samples, reagents). Not required for experienced CF investigators. Dependent (non-independent) faculty must supply a letter of support and biosketch from their laboratory PI, or the application may be withdrawn
Critique Response (upload; template) — REQUIRED IF RESUBMISSION. Point-by-point, no page limit
Assurance Statement(s) tab — applicant initials, then Authorized Institution Official initials; AIO clicks 'Submit to CFF' to complete submission

MECHANISM-SPECIFIC ADDITIONS. Training/career awards: Training Plan, Mentor's Results of Past and Current CFF/CFFT Support. Clinical Research Award: Letter of Intent package first (LOI Project Description, LOI Budget Justification, biosketches, Response to Prior LOI Critique <=3 pp), then in the full application a Protocol Synopsis, Data Safety Monitoring Plan (if applicable), Statement of Community Engagement (if applicable), Health Experiences and Outcomes Supplement (if applicable), CF Foundation Patient Registry data application and confidentiality agreement (if applicable), CFF Biorepository specimen request confirmation letter (if applicable — finalize the request at least 6 weeks before the full-application deadline), Collaboration Detail, and up to 3 reprints
result.program_officer_norms:
EXPECTED — and for CFF, uniquely, sometimes formally REQUIRED. This funder sits closer to the NIH end than the "please don't call us" foundation end, and in several documented situations skipping the PO makes your application administratively ineligible or gets it withdrawn. Contact them.

FIVE SITUATIONS WHERE PO CONTACT IS MANDATORY (each verbatim from the RFAs):
1. Heavily CFF-funded PIs. "PIs with a combined total of CF Foundation research support exceeding $200,000 per year in direct costs (excluding Research Development Program, National Resource Center, Therapeutic Development Network, and Care Center Awards) with an end date more than six (6) months from the application deadline must receive Program Officer approval before an application will be considered."
2. For-profit applicants. "Prior to beginning an application, applicants must contact the Program Officer found in Section XII to discuss eligibility. Failure to do so may result in withdrawal of the proposal."
3. A third submission. Exceptions to the two-cycle cap are available "for tenure-track PIs who are pre-tenure with prior approval from the Program Officer."
4. Off-priority clinical projects. "Projects that do not directly align with the RFA topics may be considered on a case-by-case basis and require approval from the program officer prior to submission of a letter of intent. Applications that do not align with 2027 Clinical Research Program RFA Topics without approval from the program officer may result in the administrative withdrawal of the proposal."
5. Any deviation from the guidelines. "Specific requests regarding a deviation from these guidelines must be submitted to the Program Officer Dara Riva (driva@cff.org) for approval prior to submitting their application."

EXPLICIT ENCOURAGEMENT ELSEWHERE:
- Clinical Research Award: "It is recommended that applicants speak with program staff prior to submission of a letter of intent to ensure the project design is in line with the goals of this RFA."
- Deprioritized topics: "Please reach out to CF Foundation program officers for further information."
- CFF/NIH R01-Unfunded: "Investigators with questions about their eligibility or chance of success within this program are encouraged to reach out to the program officer."
- LOI bypass: email grants@cff.org with "Clinical Research Award LOI Bypass Request" in the subject line; "LOI bypasses are granted on a case-by-case basis."
- Every mechanism page ends with the same invitation: contact GCMA "to get further information or discuss the potential relevance of their studies or research."

WHEN IN THE CYCLE: before you write, not after. The RFA publishes only ~2 months before the deadline, and the mandatory approvals above are eligibility prerequisites, so the useful window is when the prior cycle's RFA is still the best available guide — roughly 3-4 months out. For clinical awards, before the LOI, which is itself 4.5 months before the full application.

WHO TO WRITE TO (from the current Section XII contact blocks):
- Katherine Tuggle, Ph.D. — ktuggle@cff.org — scientific/programmatic PO for Research Grants, Pilot & Feasibility and Postdoctoral Fellowships, all non-infection projects
- Rebekah Dedrick, Ph.D. — rdedrick@cff.org — all infection-related projects
- Dara Riva, M.S. — driva@cff.org — Clinical Research Award and clinical programs
- Elizabeth Yu, Ph.D. — eyu@cff.org — Harry Shwachman / career-development scientific questions
- Mike Carlino — MCarlino@cff.org, 301-841-2614 — GCMA pre-award, technical AND content, for Research Grant / P&F / Postdoc
- Angela Minucci — aminucci@cff.org — pre-award manager, Clinical Research Award
- Jodie Chan — jchan@cff.org — pre-award specialist, CFF/NIH R01-Unfunded
- Erik Warnke — ewarnke@cff.org, 301-841-2614 — Harry Shwachman technical/content
- Don't know who? grants@cff.org. CFF's own instruction: contact GCMA "to find out more about specific programs and be directed to the appropriate program officer."

WHAT EXPERIENCED APPLICANTS ACTUALLY ASK: (a) Is my question inside this cycle's priority list, or will it be triaged to the abbreviated review? (b) Which mechanism — Research Grant vs Path to a Cure vs Clinical P&F vs CRA? Misrouting is the single most common fatal error, since interventional work and Patient Registry studies are simply not reviewable under the Research Grant. (c) Am I over the $168k/$200k CFF-support ceilings? (d) Can I bypass the LOI? (e) Does my NIH impact score (1-45) qualify for the R01-Unfunded bridge? (f) As a pre-tenure PI, may I have a third submission? (g) May I deviate from a formatting or content requirement?
result.funded_examples_source:
NO PUBLIC ABSTRACT DATABASE. There is no CFF equivalent of NIH RePORTER or NSF Award Search; awards.cff.org is login-gated and shows only open opportunities and your own applications. (Established by searching CFF's site and the search index rather than by a CFF statement to that effect — see `unresolved`.) The four routes that DO work, best first:

1. EUROPE PMC GRANT SEARCH — the closest thing to a CFF RePORTER, and it works today. Query GRANT_AGENCY:"Cystic Fibrosis Foundation". Verified live 2026-09-18 via the Europe PMC REST API: 3,598 records. Each record carries the CFF award ID in the format SURNAME + two-digit year + code (real examples returned: DUNCAN24G0, MCGARRY23Y5, MCGARR20A0-KB). This tells you exactly who CFF funded, in what year, on what topic — and lets you read the papers that came out of the award, which is the closest public proxy for a funded aims page. Browse: https://europepmc.org/search?query=GRANT_AGENCY%3A%22Cystic%20Fibrosis%20Foundation%22 ; API: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=GRANT_AGENCY:%22Cystic+Fibrosis+Foundation%22&format=json&resultType=core . PubMed's "Grants and funding" field carries the same data for indexed papers.

2. YOUR OWN CRITIQUES — and your colleagues'. CFF returns reviewer feedback to every applicant: "the Foundation GCMA department will notify applicants of their status and will provide anonymized reviewer critiques" (How We Fund Research). This is the summary-statement analogue. It is not public, so the move is to ask a CF-funded colleague in your department to show you theirs plus the funded application — which is how people actually calibrate for this funder. There is no university-research-office library of published CFF sample applications that I could find.

3. FORM 990 SCHEDULE I — who got money and how much, institution level. ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer, CFF EIN 13-1930701: https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/131930701 (Form 990 filings 2011-2024 available; Schedule I inside the full filing PDFs lists grants to organizations with amounts and purpose). No abstracts, but it is authoritative on scale and institutional distribution.

4. THE TEMPLATES ARE THE REAL STARTER KIT. Because there are no published sample applications, CFF's own scaffolding is what you work from, and it is unusually prescriptive: every uploaded component has a downloadable template inside awards.cff.org (Research Plan, Budget Justification, Biosketch, Other Support, Facilities Available, Results of Past and Current CFF/CFFT Support, Critique Response). Publicly, before you have an account: the "For Applicants: Our Grants Management System" how-to guide PDF and a three-part video tutorial series, both linked from https://www.cff.org/researchers/information-applicants-and-awardees ; and every mechanism's full Policies & Guidelines PDF, which contains the section-by-section content spec and — most usefully — the RFA's own "Chief causes for assigning low priority scores," which is effectively a published reviewer checklist. Subscribe to the Funding Opportunities newsletter at https://signup.e2ma.net/signup/1941850/1922653/ to be told when each cycle's RFA drops.

5. BASE RATES for expectation-setting: only the Clinical Research Award publishes them — ~35% of investigators invited to submit a full application, ~20% of full applications funded.
result.months_submission_to_award:
4 to 6 months from full-application deadline to earliest project start, depending on track; 9 months if you count from the LOI on the clinical track. CFF's own umbrella statement, covering submission to notification only: "The application review process includes multiple steps and can take anywhere from four to eight months from application submission to notification depending on the RFA."

Measured from the published Key Dates tables:
- Basic science and postdoctoral (Research Grant, P&F, Postdoc, PTAC variants), Spring 2026: deadline 12 May 2026 → committee review Aug 2026 (3.0 mo) → notification Sept 2026 (4.0 mo) → earliest start 1 Nov 2026 (5.6 mo).
- Same family, Fall 2025: deadline 9 Dec 2025 → review Mar 2026 (2.8 mo) → notification Apr 2026 (3.8 mo) → earliest start 1 May 2026 (4.7 mo).
- Career development (Harry Shwachman), 2026: deadline 25 Feb 2026 → review May 2026 (2.4 mo) → notification late May 2026 (3.0 mo) → earliest start 1 Jul 2026 (4.2 mo). Fastest track.
- Clinical, two-stage (CRA / Clinical P&F), Spring 2027: LOI 1 Oct 2026 → LOI decision Dec 2026 (2.0 mo) → full application 17 Feb 2027 (4.6 mo from LOI) → committee review Apr 2027 → notification May 2027 (3.1 mo from full app; 7.2 mo from LOI) → earliest start 1 Jul 2027 (4.4 mo from full app; 9.0 mo from LOI). Slowest track.

Planning consequence: add the ~2-month pre-deadline RFA window at the front (you cannot write to the current priority list before the RFA publishes), and the AIO countersignature plus two-week pre-registration at the back end of writing. So a realistic first-time end-to-end horizon is ~7 months for basic science and ~12 months for a clinical award. Money does not move until IRB/IACUC/IBC approvals and the institutional W-9 + 501(c)(3) (or W-8BEN-E) are on file with GCMA, so that paperwork should run during the review wait, not after notification.

result.funder_system: Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation — a private non-profit (One Exchange Plaza, 55 Broadway, Suite 302, New York, NY 10006; awards@damonrunyon.org; 212.455.0520). Eight award programs share ONE application machine, which is why it is worth learning once: (1) Fellowship Award (postdoc, 4 yr, $300,000); (2) Damon Runyon–St. Jude Pediatric Cancer Research Fellowship (postdoc, 4 yr); (3) Quantitative Biology Fellowship (postdoc from math/CS/physics/engineering, 3 yr, $240,000, requires TWO mentors — one dry lab, one wet lab); (4) Damon Runyon–Rachleff Innovation Award (early-career faculty / distinguished fellows, 2 yr $400,000 + possible 2-yr continuation to $800,000); (5) Clinical Investigator Award (junior physician-scientist faculty, 3 yr $600,000 + continuation, + up to $100,000 med-school debt retirement); (6) Physician-Scientist Training Award (MD only, cannot be pursuing a PhD; 4 yr $460,000 + debt retirement); (7) Dale F. Frey Award for Breakthrough Scientists (open ONLY to current Damon Runyon Fellows/Quant Bio Fellows in their 4th year; 2 yr, $100,000); (8) SPARK post-bac program ($61,000/yr, college seniors and recent BA/BS grads). House rules that hold across all of them: everything goes through ProposalCentral; every deadline is 4:00 PM Eastern; review is by a standing, program-specific committee of outside scientists whose picks are approved by the Board of Directors (no NIH-style council); "No part of this grant can be used for indirect costs or institutional overhead"; and "it is the policy of the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation not to share reviewers' written comments." Non-US citizens may apply if the work is done at a US institution; US citizens may propose work abroad only with an exceptional justification. Sources: funder's own pages, fetched directly (no search-index substitution needed — damonrunyon.org serves plain fetches fine).
result.submission_portal:
ProposalCentral (Altum), https://proposalcentral.com — every Damon Runyon program, no exceptions. The funder's wording: "To apply, please log into Altum | Proposal Central and search for Damon Runyon Fellowship Award" and "No hard copies or emailed applications will be accepted." Advance registration needed: a free ProposalCentral applicant account plus your Professional Profile; then search the program by name and click Apply Now. ProposalCentral applicant support: pcsupport@altum.com, 800.875.2562 (US/Canada) or +1.703.964.5840, 8:30am–5:00pm ET Mon–Fri.

THE TWO REAL LONG-LEAD ITEMS (this is what first-timers miss):
(1) Reference letters are a hard submit-gate, not a courtesy. "In Section 7 of the application, the applicant will put in the referees' email addresses. Referees will receive an email from Proposal Central, which will give them access to the reference letter portal where they will upload their letter." And: "Applicants will NOT be able to submit their application unless all reference letters are uploaded to the portal." The fellowships need THREE (from people other than your Sponsor; for PhD candidates one MUST be the thesis advisor; "Reference letters should be two to three pages in length"). Innovation/Clinical Investigator/PSTA/Frey need TWO. So referees must be asked ~4–6 weeks out, and chased.
(2) Clinical Investigator Award only — institutional nomination, which adds 2–3 months upstream. Funder's words: "Each applicant must be nominated by their institution. Applications will only be accepted from institutions that have been invited to submit them by the Foundation (See list). Three (3) nominations per institution, including its affiliated schools, will be accepted." The page carries a banner: "NOTICE: Institutional nominations have been reinstated. Please review carefully." The invited list is a 12-page PDF updated June 2026 (https://www.damonrunyon.org/sites/default/files/2026-06/CIA%20Invited%20Institutions%20UPDATED%20-%20JUNE%202026.pdf), organized by state, covering 45 states + DC and roughly 149 institutions (count is mine from the PDF text; the PDF states no total). If your institution is on it, your research-development / limited-submission office runs an internal competition first. Illustrative (older cycle, and under the previous 5-nomination cap): MGH ECOR ran an internal LOI of 2–3 pages plus an NIH biosketch to ecor@mgh.harvard.edu, due "Wednesday, November 13, 2024 at 5:00pm" for a February funder deadline — i.e. the internal deadline lands ~2.5 months before Damon Runyon's.

Also portal-shaped: the Application Cover Sheet needs institutional signatures (electronic/scanned) — route it to your grants office early; the Summary of Research Form must match the Abstracts tab in ProposalCentral; and for Innovation co-applicants, ProposalCentral cannot take two sets of referee letters, so one co-applicant's referees email awards@damonrunyon.org directly with the subject line "Reference Letter for [name], joint application with [name]".
result.deadline_structure:
FIXED ANNUAL (or semi-annual) DATES per program. Not rolling, not per-solicitation, no LOI/pre-application stage (except the CIA institutional nomination).

On the "no dated deadline" question: this funder is the clearest case for recording BOTH layers, because it publishes both and they currently disagree. (a) The evergreen anchor lives in the FAQ "Fast Facts" table; (b) the operative dated deadline lives on each program's own Application Guidelines page. A dated deadline alone rots in twelve months; an anchor alone is wrong by up to two weeks and will make someone miss a cycle. Record anchor + dated deadline + a "verified on" stamp (these were verified 2026-09-18), and always point the reader at the program page as the authority.

ANCHORS (FAQ "Fast Facts", https://www.damonrunyon.org/for-scientists/faq): Clinical Investigator — February 1; Fellowship — March 15 and August 15; Dale F. Frey — July 15; Rachleff Innovation — July 1; Physician-Scientist Training — December 1; Quantitative Biology — December 1.

result.months_submission_to_award: Decision in 2-4.5 months; money in 3.5-7 months. Per mechanism, submission to earliest start: Fellowship 4.5-7.5 months (Aug cycle) or 3.5-6.5 months (Mar cycle); St. Jude Pediatric Fellowship 4.5-7.5 months; Quantitative Biology 4-6 months; Rachleff Innovation 6 months; Clinical Investigator 5.4 months; Physician-Scientist Training 7 months; Dale F. Frey continuous with the ending Fellowship. Notification comes much earlier than the start date: 2.5-3 months for the non-interview fellowships ("in the week following the selection meeting"), 3.5-4.5 months for the interview programs. Planning number for a first-timer: start assembling ~3 months before the deadline (4-6 months for the Clinical Investigator Award, because of the institutional nomination), and expect roughly a year from "I should apply for this" to first dollar.
result.resubmission_policy:
Allowed once for almost everything; never for the Frey Award. The FAQ "Fast Facts" row "Number of reapplications allowed (if still otherwise eligible)" reads: Clinical Investigator 1, Fellowship 1, Dale F. Frey 0, Rachleff Innovation 1, Physician-Scientist Training 1, Quantitative Biology 1. The program pages state the same rule as a lifetime cap on attempts: Innovation — "Applicants may apply no more than two times."; Clinical Investigator — "Candidates may apply up to two times during this eligibility period."; PSTA — "Eligible candidates may apply up to two times." For the Frey Award the funder is explicit: Damon Runyon Fellows "are eligible to apply for the Dale F. Frey Award one time only, in the fourth year of their award."

INTRODUCTION PAGE EQUIVALENT — yes, but shorter than NIH's and only stated for two programs. Rachleff Innovation: "If applicable, candidates resubmitting an application must upload a Resubmission Summary of Changes, a brief paragraph outlining the changes or updates made to the current proposal compared to the previous proposal. This paragraph should be attached as a preface to the Research Proposal. This summary should not exceed half a page." The Clinical Investigator guidelines carry the same requirement, without the half-page/preface wording. The Fellowship, St. Jude, Quantitative Biology and PSTA requirement lists do not mention a resubmission summary — treat that as "not stated", not "not required", and ask awards@damonrunyon.org.

TIME WINDOW — there is no separate resubmission clock; the binding constraint is the ordinary eligibility clock, which keeps moving. A Fellowship resubmission only works if your degree-conferral date is still inside the window for the new deadline (e.g. "February 14, 2025 - August 14, 2026" for the Aug 2026 cycle) and you have not been in the Sponsor's lab too long; a CIA or Innovation resubmission must still be inside the years-since-appointment window. Practically: for the fellowships you usually get exactly one retry, at the next semi-annual deadline, before aging out.

PER-SESSION CROWDING RULES that can block a resubmission even when you are eligible: Fellowship — "Only one fellowship application will be accepted from a Sponsor or Fellow per review session (including Co-Sponsors); there is no limit, however, to the number of applications from an institution", and "No more than two Damon Runyon Fellows will be funded to work with the same Sponsor at any given time". CIA and PSTA — "Only one application will be accepted from a Mentor per review session." CIA additionally — three nominations per institution per cycle.

THE HARD PART: you must revise blind. Damon Runyon releases no scores and no written critiques, so a resubmission has to be improved from the guidelines, your mentors, and people in your department who have served on or won the award — there is no summary statement to respond to.
result.page_limits:
CONSTANT ACROSS MECHANISMS: single-spaced, 12-point type, at least 0.5-inch margins; figures, tables and legends must fit INSIDE the proposal page limit; references are excluded from it and must give full titles. Summary of Research Form: not to exceed one page (and must match the Abstracts tab in ProposalCentral). Personal statement: one page. Biosketch: current NIH format. Bibliography: a separate hyperlinked list in addition to the biosketch (bioRxiv preprints allowed). Collaboration letters: one page each, and explicitly "NOT REFERENCE LETTERS".

RESEARCH PROPOSAL, by mechanism: Fellowship 5 pages; Damon Runyon-St. Jude Pediatric Fellowship 5 pages; Quantitative Biology Fellowship 5 pages; Clinical Investigator Award 5 pages; Physician-Scientist Training Award 4 pages; Rachleff Innovation 4 pages ("No preliminary data are expected; any description of such data (including figures) should be included in the four-page proposal").

MENTOR/SPONSOR DOCUMENT, by mechanism: Fellowship and St. Jude — "Sponsor's comprehensive and detailed training plan for the candidate, up to two pages" (one joint plan if two Sponsors); Quantitative Biology — a single jointly written training plan up to two pages from the two Mentors, which must argue the dry-lab/wet-lab pairing; Clinical Investigator — Mentor's Proposal for Training, 3 pages (4 if two mentors); PSTA — Mentor's Proposal for Training, 3 pages.

APPLICANT NARRATIVE, by mechanism: Fellowship / St. Jude / Quant Bio — applicant's letter "approximately two pages" (prior research, teaching, transformative impact as a graduate student, plus a required explanation if you are staying at your degree institution), personal statement 1 page, long-term commitment statement "no longer than one paragraph". St. Jude adds a pediatric impact statement "not exceeding 300 words". Quant Bio adds an innovation paragraph "no more than 250 words" and a computational-challenges paragraph "no more than 250 words". Innovation — personal statement 1 page, bibliography with exactly three publications bolded. PSTA — applicant's letter on long-term vision, personal statement 1 page, plus "Accomplishments (3 most important)". Resubmission Summary of Changes (Innovation): half a page maximum. SPARK — CV 3 pages, personal statement 1 page, commitment-to-research statement 1 page, research interest 1 paragraph.

REFERENCE LETTERS: fellowships 3 (from people other than the Sponsor/Mentor; one must be the PhD thesis advisor; "two to three pages in length"); Innovation, CIA, PSTA, Frey 2. Innovation adds a constraint worth planning around: one of the two must come from "a senior scientist, external to the candidate's institution" who "may not be a collaborator, coauthor, or current/former mentor of the applicant".

HARD PROHIBITIONS that read like page limits but are eligibility bars: for the Fellowship, "Proposals to continue training in the laboratory where the applicant received their PhD will not be considered. Proposals that are direct extensions of graduate work will not be funded."

result.program_officer_norms:
There are no program officers here, and no pre-submission fit conversation. This is the opposite pole from NIH and it is the single biggest expectation to reset for anyone whose only model is an NIH PO.

What exists instead: one central Award Programs mailbox, awards@damonrunyon.org, and one phone number, 212.455.0520 ("Contact us with other awards-related questions at awards@damonrunyon.org or 212.455.0520"). Every program page, from Fellowship to SPARK, lists the same address. No individual staff contact is published — the /about/our-team URL returns 404 — and there is no assigned officer for your application.

Contact is TOLERATED AND EXPLICITLY INVITED, but only on narrow factual matters, and the site shows you which ones: eligibility and concurrent funding ("Please contact the Foundation with any questions regarding concurrent funding (212.455.0520)"), allowable use of funds ("If you have any questions on how the money may be spent, please contact the Foundation (awards@damonrunyon.org)"), your DRG number for acknowledgements, and portal mechanics such as the co-applicant reference-letter workaround (referees email awards@damonrunyon.org with a prescribed subject line). Nothing on the site offers scientific advice, project-fit triage, or a look at a draft.

WHEN: as early as possible, and before you start writing — because Damon Runyon's eligibility rules are date arithmetic, not judgement calls, and one wrong date voids the whole effort. The questions experienced applicants actually ask: does my degree-conferral date fall inside this cycle's window (and does a delayed diploma count if I have defended); how is "time in the Sponsor's lab" counted for me; can I hold a T32 (yes at application, not concurrently) or a K award (K12 can be turned back; NIH K holders are ineligible for the Fellowship); does my start-up package or pending grant create budgetary overlap; is my institution on the CIA invited list and who controls our three nominations; can I apply to two programs in the same season (stated only for the August Fellowship vs St. Jude pair — you must choose one).

WHAT NOT TO EXPECT: no reviewer comments, ever ("it is the policy of the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation not to share reviewers' written comments"), so there is no post-decision debrief call. No negotiation of terms: "The Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation will not modify the terms of its policies at the request of individual institutions." No published webinar or office-hours program for the research awards; the only applicant-facing information session located anywhere was for SPARK, the post-baccalaureate program.

WHO TO TALK TO INSTEAD — this matters for a first-timer and the funder effectively designates them: (1) your Sponsor/Mentor, who is co-author of the application in all but name (training plan, mentorship track record, letter of support) and whose track record is a scored criterion; (2) your institution's research development or limited-submission office, which is the mandatory gate for the Clinical Investigator Award and the place that holds internal deadlines and past applications; (3) Damon Runyon awardees in your own department or city, findable through the Foundation's Current Projects database filtered by geography — they are the only realistic source of a real successful application; (4) the published selection committee rosters (https://www.damonrunyon.org/for-scientists/award-selection-committees), which tell you exactly which scientists will read your proposal, a better targeting instrument than any conversation with staff.
result.funded_examples_source:
No RePORTER equivalent and no public full applications — Damon Runyon publishes no scores, no summary statements and no application texts. What IS public, and is genuinely usable:

1. CURRENT PROJECTS DATABASE — the closest thing to funded abstracts. Browse by award program at https://www.damonrunyon.org/our-impact/current-projects/award-program (filters: /award-program/fellow, /innovator, /clinical%20investigator, /physician-scientist, /quantitative%20biology%20fellow, /st.%20jude, /dale%20frey%20scientist, /SPARK%20Scholar), by disease at https://www.damonrunyon.org/our-impact/current-projects/cancer-type (e.g. .../cancer-type/lung-cancer), or by geography at https://www.damonrunyon.org/our-impact/current-projects/geography. Every entry carries scientist name, institution, award program, named award, cancer type, research area, project title and a short project description written for an intermediate-scientific audience — e.g. Jinho D. Jeong, PhD (Massachusetts General Hospital, Fellow, Robert Black Fellow), "A Systematic Approach for Targeting Protein Complexes in Lung Cancer". Individual pages sit at https://www.damonrunyon.org/our-impact/current-projects/scientists/<id> — for example .../5756 (Jingchuan Luo, HHMI Fellow, Sponsor Jonathan S. Weissman, Whitehead Institute: "Deciphering roles of nuclear-mitochondrial communication in cellular homeostasis") and .../3321 (Lydia Finley).

2. WHY THOSE BLURBS ARE WORTH IMITATING: they are downstream of a reporting requirement — awardees must submit "Two abstracts (one lay and one scientific) of their accomplishments over the term of the award", and annual reports require "A brief, lay abstract... The lay summary should not exceed one page." Writing your one-page Summary of Research Form in that register is cheap alignment with how the Foundation talks about its own science.

3. AWARD ANNOUNCEMENT NEWS RELEASES — each new class is announced with per-awardee project blurbs, sponsor and institution, at https://www.damonrunyon.org/news (e.g. "Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation awards Fellowships to 15 brilliant young scientists"). Useful for calibrating what a winning career stage and project scale look like, and for finding people to ask.

4. SELECTION COMMITTEE ROSTERS — https://www.damonrunyon.org/for-scientists/award-selection-committees and per-program pages such as https://www.damonrunyon.org/for-scientists/committees/clinical-investigator. Named reviewers; read their work before you write.

5. FOR ACTUAL APPLICATION TEXT you must go offline: your institution's research development office (many keep files of funded applications), your Sponsor, or a current/former Damon Runyon Fellow in your department located via the geography filter above. A targeted search of university sites turned up many pages summarizing eligibility and deadlines (Harvard FAS Research Administration, UChicago GRAD, UCI, Caltech, MSU, USC Keck) but no publicly posted sample Damon Runyon application. Treat "no public sample exists" as established for the open web and "ask your RD office" as the working route.
