result.funder_system:
The Pew Charitable Trusts — NOT a single application system. It is three separate machineries under one brand, and a first-time applicant must identify which one applies before anything else:

(A) PEW BIOMEDICAL PROGRAMS (Philadelphia office, staff at 215-575-xxxx). Four mechanisms sharing one machinery, one portal and one annual calendar:
 - Pew Biomedical Scholars ($306,000 = $75,000/yr x 4 + $6,000 travel stipend at $1,500/yr; ~21-22 awards/yr; founded 1985). Assistant professors in their first 3 years.
 - Pew-Stewart Scholars for Cancer Research (same $306,000 terms; ~5 awards/yr; founded 2014 with the Alexander and Margaret Stewart Trust). Cancer-focused; 95 participating cancer centers.
 - Pew Latin American Fellows ($30,000/yr stipend x 2 yrs + $70,000 lab-startup payment on return to Latin America + $4,500 travel; 10 awards/yr; founded 1990/91). Postdoc fellowship.
 - Pew Innovation Fund (alumni-only; pairs of Pew biomedical alumni at assistant professor or above; 7-8 pairs/yr; launched 2017, supported by the Kathryn W. Davis Peace by Pieces Fund and in part by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative Foundation).

(B) PEW MARINE FELLOWS / Pew Fellows Program in Marine Conservation ($150,000 over 3 years; ~7 awards/yr; 221 fellows in 45 countries to date). Midcareer, global, environmental-science division. Entirely closed nomination.

(C) THE PEW CENTER FOR ARTS & HERITAGE (pewcenterarts.org) — a legally and operationally separate grantmaker, Philadelphia five-county region only, own staff, own portal, own calendar, own panels. Creative Project grants, Evolving Futures grants, Capacity Building grants (organizations, 501(c)(3), min. $150k annual expenses), and Pew Fellowships in the Arts ($85,000 unrestricted to 12 artists/yr, nomination-only). Do not confuse this with (A) or (B).

(D) A fourth, minor arm: procurement-style RFPs/RFIs listed at pew.org/en/about/current-contract-and-grant-opportunities, run by contracts and procurement services (Pew_RFP_SCP@pewtrusts.org), per-solicitation deadlines. Not a research-grant route.

THE STRUCTURAL FACT THAT DEFINES THIS FUNDER: for (A) and (B) there is no open call. You cannot self-apply to Pew Biomedical Scholars, Pew-Stewart, Pew Marine Fellows, the Innovation Fund, or Pew Fellowships in the Arts. Pew Latin American Fellows is the ONE biomedical mechanism an individual can enter unaided — you email the program office for portal access. Everything else runs through an institutional or expert nominator.

DOMAIN MIGRATION (drift warning): pewtrusts.org now 301-redirects to pew.org, and the site was recently redesigned ("We've recently redesigned our website"). Many university and third-party pages still cite pewtrusts.org paths; several old project paths (e.g. /en/projects/pew-fellows-program-in-marine-conservation) now 404 — marine fellows live at /en/projects/marine-fellows. Email addresses, however, remain @pewtrusts.org.
result.submission_portal:
BIOMEDICAL PROGRAMS (Scholars, Pew-Stewart, Latin American Fellows): a Pew-operated online grant application portal. There is NO self-registration and no public URL. Credentials are emailed by the program office directly to eligible applicants:
- Pew Scholars / Pew-Stewart: "The Pew program office will email grant application portal login information and a detailed application guide directly to all nominated applicants by June 10, 2026. The online application website will open on June 10, 2026." Research administrators get access by emailing scholarsapp@pewtrusts.org (or Pew-Stewart@pewtrusts.org) with the applicant cc'd, and only AFTER June 10 — "No requests will be accepted prior to this date."
- Latin American Fellows: the applicant themselves emails fellowsapp@pewtrusts.org on or after June 3, 2026 to request login information. This is the only self-initiated route in the biomedical family.

THE HIDDEN LONG-LEAD ITEM IS NOT AN ACCOUNT — IT IS THE NOMINATION. For Scholars/Pew-Stewart the real long-lead item is your own institution's internal limited-submission competition, which runs 6-10 weeks BEFORE Pew's nomination deadline and is where most candidates are actually eliminated. Observed internal deadlines for the 2027 cycle: BU March 10, 2026 (via InfoReady Review); Weill Cornell March 30, 2026; CU Boulder April 6, 2026; Dana-Farber/Harvard Cancer Consortium May 4, 2026. Find your research development or limited-submissions office in January-February, not April. For Latin American Fellows the long-lead item is instead securing a US sponsor lab, which Pew says "may require a significant time commitment and take several months."

I could NOT establish the portal's software vendor. Probing pewtrusts.smartsimple.com returned SmartSimple's generic "portal not found" catch-all page, and apply.pewscholars.org (surfaced by a search index as a legacy Pew application host) refused a connection on port 443. Both are tooling facts and establish nothing either way.

PEW CENTER FOR ARTS & HERITAGE: a genuinely separate, self-service portal at https://apply.pewcenterarts.org/login with a public "Register Now" for Project Grant Applicants. Entry is via a short Initial Inquiry Form that "does not require an online account"; the portal link arrives after that form. Financial documents go to a "My Financials" tab in the portal. Existing grantees manage open grants in a separate GivingData Grantee Portal. Capacity-building Research and Travel requests use a Cognito Forms form. Contact apply@pewcenterarts.org.

MARINE FELLOWS: no portal is public. Nominees are invited by Pew and given application access; "unsolicited applications are not accepted." Contact marinefellows@pewtrusts.org.

NOTE ON METHOD: pew.org returns HTTP 403 to a plain fetch on several project pages (program-details in particular). All pew.org content above was read with a rendering browser. The university pages (BU, Weill Cornell, Penn State, DF/HCC, CU Boulder) were located via a search index, then read directly.
result.deadline_structure:
FIXED, RECURRING, ANNUAL — and the dates barely move year to year. This is a funder where you can plan a year ahead. Pew publishes hard calendar dates on its own site; they are quoted verbatim below.

PEW BIOMEDICAL SCHOLARS — 2027 class (Pew's own wording):
- Early April 2026 — "a letter of invitation and application instructions will be sent to the leaders and offices of sponsored research of the institutions invited to nominate a candidate"
- May 13, 2026 — institutional nomination due. "Nominations of applicants to the program will not be considered after May 13, 2026."
- June 10, 2026 — portal opens; login + detailed application guide emailed to nominees
- Sept. 3, 2026 — "The application submission deadline is Sept. 3, 2026."
- April 2027 — National Advisory Committee recommends to the Pew board; candidates notified
- June 2027 — public announcement
- August 2027 — grant agreements issued

PEW-STEWART SCHOLARS — 2027 class: identical except the application deadline: "The application submission deadline is Aug. 27, 2026." Invitation early April 2026; nomination May 13, 2026; portal opens June 10, 2026; notification April 2027; announcement June 2027; agreements August 2027.

PEW LATIN AMERICAN FELLOWS — 2027 class: "The application portal opens on June 3, 2026." / "Applications must be submitted electronically by 5 p.m. ET on Aug. 19, 2026." (Note: this is the only Pew biomedical deadline with a published clock time.) Notification April 2027; board approval and announcement June 2027; grant to the US sponsoring institution August 2027.

THE RECURRING SHAPE (stable across cycles — the 2026 cycle ran nomination May 14, 2025 / deadline Sept. 3, 2025; the 2024 cycle ran nomination May 17, 2023 / portal June 12, 2023 / Pew-Stewart Aug. 31, 2023 / Scholars Sept. 7, 2023):
- Institutional invitation: early April
- Institutional nomination: mid-May (2nd or 3rd Wednesday)
- Portal opens: ~June 10
- Pew-Stewart closes: late August
- Pew Scholars closes: first week of September
- Latin American Fellows: portal early June, closes mid-to-late August
- Notification: April, ~7-8 months later
- Public announcement: June
- Money: August

THE TRAP MOST APPLICANTS MISS: reference letters are due TWO WEEKS BEFORE the application deadline, not on it. Pew's own program-officer deck states for the 2024 cycle: "August 31, 2023 Pew-Stewart application closes (*reference letters due 2 weeks prior)" and "September 7, 2023 Pew scholar application closes (*reference letters due 2 weeks prior)"; for Latin American Fellows, "August 2, 2023 Reference and sponsor letters due (2 weeks prior to deadline)". Applying the same rule to the 2027 cycle puts letters around Aug. 20, 2026 (Scholars), Aug. 13, 2026 (Pew-Stewart) and Aug. 5, 2026 (Latin American) — but I could NOT find those exact 2027 letter dates published; they are in the application guide issued with portal access. Ask your referees in June, not August.

PEW MARINE FELLOWS: no deadlines published anywhere. Awards are announced each March (2026 class announced March 11, 2026). Nomination and application dates are communicated privately to invited nominators and nominees.

PEW INNOVATION FUND: no deadlines published. Classes are announced each December (2024 class Dec. 10, 2024; 2025 class Dec. 9, 2025). Solicited from alumni directly.

PEW CENTER FOR ARTS & HERITAGE — 2026 cycle (separate calendar, and note this one uses a multi-stage funnel):
- Feb. 3, 2026 — cycle opens, guidelines published
- March 16, 2026 — Initial Inquiry Form due; financial documents due to the portal's "My Financials" tab
- March 27, 2026 — staff meetings for organizations new to the process or that have not applied since 2020 (optional for returning applicants)
- April 9, 2026, 4 p.m. EST — Letters of Intent (Creative Project) / project briefs (Evolving Futures) due
- May 28, 2026 — applicants notified whether they proceed to full application
- June 2026 — technical assistance grants ($500-$1,500) open to those invited to full application
Applicants may apply for only one grant type per cycle.

PROCUREMENT RFPs/RFIs: per-solicitation. Example live at time of research: "Facilitating Evidence Synthesis to Improve Decision-Making on Endocrine-Disrupting Chemicals" — Release April 14, 2026; questions April 27, 2026; proposals June 15, 2026.

review_stages.stage: Institutional invitation issued to the 212 participating institutions (Scholars) / 95 cancer centers (Pew-Stewart). Your institution's sponsored research office distributes it campus-wide.
review_stages.timing: Early April, ~17 months before the award starts

review_stages.stage: Internal limited-submission competition at your own institution. An internal committee picks ONE nominee. Pew: 'The individual chosen for the institutional nomination is guaranteed an application to the program.' This is the single highest-attrition stage and it is invisible on Pew's website.
review_stages.timing: March-early May; internal deadlines run 6-10 weeks before Pew's

review_stages.stage: PARALLEL ROUTE — alumni nomination. Pew separately solicits all Pew alumni to nominate individuals. 'Nominees do not participate in the nomination process. Nominees are not guaranteed an automatic application. Nominations are reviewed by a board of Pew alumni and a subset are invited to apply.'
review_stages.timing: Same spring window

review_stages.stage: Institutional nomination filed with Pew: a member of the internal selection committee completes an online survey describing the selection process used and submits the nominee's name and contact details.
review_stages.timing: May 13, 2026 (hard cutoff)

review_stages.stage: Portal opens; login and detailed application guide emailed directly to nominees.
Reference letters due (3 letters) — two weeks before the application deadline.
review_stages.timing: ~2 weeks before close; mid-to-late August

review_stages.stage: Application closes.
review_stages.timing: Aug. 27, 2026 (Pew-Stewart) / Sept. 3, 2026 (Scholars) / Aug. 19, 2026 5 p.m. ET (Latin American Fellows)

review_stages.stage: REGIONAL COMMITTEE STAGE — LATIN AMERICAN FELLOWS ONLY. Four regional committees (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Mexico) plus one covering all other countries, composed of former Pew fellows, review applications and interview shortlisted candidates in person or by video. Each region advances six candidates (~30 total). Unsuccessful candidates are notified in late October.
review_stages.timing: September-October 2026; ~1-2 months after submission

review_stages.stage: National Advisory Committee review. Scholars: an 18-member committee (currently 18 named members, chaired by Lee A. Niswander). Pew-Stewart: a separate, smaller committee. Latin American: a 12-member US committee reviewing the ~30 regional nominees. No interviews at this stage for Latin American Fellows.
review_stages.timing: Roughly September/November 2026 - February 2027, i.e. months 1-6 after submission

review_stages.stage: Final selection meeting.
review_stages.timing: March 2027, ~6 months after submission

review_stages.stage: Applicants notified of the decision; successful candidates are told they have been recommended to the Pew (and Stewart) board.
review_stages.timing: April 2027, ~7 months after submission

review_stages.stage: Pew board of directors approves grantees; public announcement.
review_stages.timing: June 2027, ~9 months after submission

review_stages.stage: Grant agreement issued to the host institution and first payment made. Earliest effective award start.
review_stages.timing: August 2027, ~11-12 months after submission

result.months_submission_to_award:
~11-12 months from application submission to money (Sept. 3, 2026 submission → August 2027 grant agreement and first payment). Intermediate milestones: ~7 months to a decision (April 2027), ~9 months to public announcement (June 2027).

Measured from the start of the process the lead time is much longer, and this is the number to plan against:
- From your institution's internal deadline (March-early May 2026) to money: ~15-17 months.
- From Pew's institutional invitation (early April 2026) to money: ~16 months.
- Latin American Fellows: Aug. 19, 2026 submission → April 2027 notification (~8 months) → August 2027 grant and lab start (~12 months). Add the sponsor-lab search, which Pew says can "take several months" and which its own timeline allocates February-June 2026 — so ~18 months end to end.

Practical consequence: if you are an assistant professor now and want Pew money in hand, you are working on a two-year horizon, and the eligibility clock (3 years since first independent appointment) is running against you the whole time. Count backwards from the award year, not forwards from today.
result.resubmission_policy:
PEW SCHOLARS and PEW-STEWART — a hard lifetime cap of two attempts per program, and no resubmission mechanics in the NIH sense. Pew's own words: "May apply to the program a maximum of two times. All applicants must be nominated by their institution and must complete the 2027 online application." Dana-Farber/HCC's reproduction of the call puts it as "Candidates may be nominated by their institution only twice."

Critical structural point: a second attempt is NOT a resubmission you control. It is a fresh nomination — your institution must choose you again over every other eligible candidate on campus, in a year when it can still nominate only one person. Many second attempts die internally and never reach Pew.

There is NO introduction page, NO response-to-reviewers section, and NO requirement to mark what changed. Pew issues no summary statement or written critique to react to. The second application is simply a new application.

Institution-shopping is explicitly blocked: "If applicants have appointments at more than one eligible nominating institution or affiliate, they may not reapply in a subsequent year from a different nominating entity." And "Candidates with dual appointments at affiliated institutions can only be nominated from one institution."

Cross-program rule — this is the one genuine second bite: "May not be nominated for the Pew Scholars Program and the Pew-Stewart Scholars Program for Cancer Research in the same year." But sequencing IS allowed: "A candidate can be nominated to Pew scholars one year and Pew-Stewart the next." So a cancer-relevant investigator has up to four shots across two programs (two each), provided the institution nominates them each time and the eligibility clock holds. One individual will not receive both awards.

THE REAL TIME WINDOW IS THE ELIGIBILITY CLOCK, NOT A RESUBMISSION RULE. For the 2027 award you "must not have been appointed as an assistant professor and run an independent lab at any institution prior to June 10, 2023" — a three-year window, and "Time limit stands regardless of changing institutions." Time in clinical internships, residencies, board certification work, or parental leave does not count. Exceptions exist but must be arranged in advance: "Candidates who need an exception on the three-year limit should contact Pew's program office to ensure that application reviewers are aware an exception has been given." Note the drift: the window was temporarily widened to four years for COVID through the 2026 competition and has now reverted to three years for 2027.

PEW LATIN AMERICAN FELLOWS — I could NOT find any published limit on the number of times a candidate may apply. Not found; treat as unknown, not as unlimited. The binding constraints are instead dates: PhD/MD awarded between June 3, 2021 and Feb. 1, 2027, and no postdoctoral training started in the US or Europe before March 1, 2025.

PEW MARINE FELLOWS — unlimited nominations, one award: "Individuals may be nominated multiple times but can be awarded the fellowship only once."

PEW FELLOWSHIPS IN THE ARTS — previous recipients are permanently ineligible.

PEW CENTER FOR ARTS & HERITAGE organizational grants — not a resubmission limit but a lockout: an organization may "Not have an open grant in the project funding area from which they seek funding" in the cycle, and may apply for only one grant type per cycle. 2025 planning-grant recipients were ineligible for 2026 implementation grants.
result.program_officer_norms:
EXPECTED AND ACTIVELY ENCOURAGED — this is an unusually open foundation, closer to NIH than to a typical closed-door private funder. Pew publishes named staff with direct phone numbers and runs formal outreach. Do not treat it like a foundation where contact is discouraged.

WHO: Pew Biomedical Programs staff are published with direct lines — Kara Coleman, Ph.D., Project Director (kcoleman@pewtrusts.org, 215-575-4925); Donna Dang, Ph.D., Principal Associate (ddang@pewtrusts.org, 215-575-4740); Sarah Kelly (skelly@pewtrusts.org, 215-575-4727); Sara Strickland, Senior Officer; Hannah Hinson. Program-level mailboxes: scholarsapp@pewtrusts.org (Scholars), Pew-Stewart@pewtrusts.org, fellowsapp@pewtrusts.org (Latin American), marinefellows@pewtrusts.org, apply@pewcenterarts.org and zblackwood@pewcenterarts.org (arts).

PEW INVITES CONTACT IN WRITING, REPEATEDLY:
- Eligibility: "If you have questions concerning eligibility, please contact Pew Biomedical Programs (scholarsapp@pewtrusts.org) in advance of applying."
- Eligibility-clock exceptions: "Candidates who need an exception on the three-year limit should contact Pew's program office to ensure that application reviewers are aware an exception has been given." This is the single highest-value call an applicant can make, and it must happen BEFORE the nomination, not after.
- Institutions: "Institutions that would like to be considered for invitation may contact scholarsapp@pewtrusts.org" — i.e. a department at a non-listed institution can ask to be added to the 212.
- Internal selection design: "For guidance on this process, please contact scholarsapp@pewtrusts.org." Pew runs "Pew office hours (for institutional selection)" and "Pew webinars (for applicants)."
- Latin American Fellows, sponsor matching: "The program office will assist with the identification of possible laboratories with matching research interests." And, explicitly, "Pew staff can also connect you with current fellows and alumni; email fellowsapp@pewtrusts.org to request an introduction." A funder that will personally introduce you to past awardees is rare — use it.

WHEN IN THE CYCLE:
- January-March: institutional/research-development questions; ask to be added to the participating list.
- Before nomination (April-early May): eligibility rulings and clock exceptions. This is the critical window.
- After June 10 only: portal access requests. "No requests will be accepted prior to this date" — sending earlier just gets you ignored.
- June-August: application-guide mechanics; attend the applicant webinar.
- Latin American Fellows: sponsor-lab help is offered "prior to June 3, 2026," i.e. before the portal even opens.

WHAT EXPERIENCED APPLICANTS ACTUALLY ASK: (1) Does my appointment date count, and can I get a documented exception for leave or a clinical track? (2) Is my appointment title eligible — the research/adjunct/instructor exclusions catch many people. (3) Is my project cancer-relevant enough for Pew-Stewart, or better placed in Scholars this year? (4) Does my other funding conflict? — the published answer is no: "Funding from the NIH, other government sources, and project grants from nonprofit associations do not pose a conflict." (5) For Latin American Fellows: is this sponsor lab strong enough, and will you introduce me to an alum in my region?

NOTE WHAT IS *NOT* AVAILABLE: Pew program officers do not review draft proposals, and there is no pre-proposal or concept-check step at Pew. Scientific triage happens inside your own institution's committee and then at the National Advisory Committee. The people to show a draft to are your institution's research development office and, better, a past Pew scholar — Pew names alumni as good internal-committee members and the directories give you their emails.

INSTITUTIONS ALSO BROKER ACCESS: Weill Cornell hosted an internal information session for the 2027 cycle featuring Pew's own Donna Dang and Sarah Kelly, with a recording. Ask your research office whether a Pew briefing is scheduled — this is routine, not a favour.

ARTS CENTER NORMS DIFFER: contact is procedural and partly mandatory. Staff meetings are required for organizations new to the process or that have not applied since 2020 (by March 27, 2026), required for all Evolving Futures applicants, and optional for returning applicants. But note that Center staff "do not serve on the Creative Project, Evolving Futures, or Pew Fellowships grant selection panels and do not determine recipients" — so staff contact is about process and fit, never influence.

MARINE FELLOWS: there is nothing to lobby for. Contact marinefellows@pewtrusts.org to learn about the program, but selection begins with an invited nominator you cannot approach through Pew.
result.funded_examples_source:
There is NO Pew equivalent of NIH RePORTER, and Pew publishes NO full funded applications and NO reviewer summary statements. What exists instead is a set of rich, searchable, lay-written funded-project abstracts plus unusually direct access to the awardees themselves.

1. PEW SCHOLARS DIRECTORY — the primary resource. https://www.pew.org/en/projects/pew-biomedical-scholars/directory-of-pew-scholars
Every scholar back to 1985 has a profile page carrying a ~200-word first-person funded-project description, research field, keywords, institution, award year, lab website AND direct email. Filterable by keyword, research field, institution, award year, state, and an "Innovation Fund Investigator" flag. URL pattern: /directory-of-pew-scholars/<year>/<name-slug>. Example (2026 scholar Corey Allard, Harvard Medical School): "My lab will explore how some sea slugs turn to thievery to gain new abilities... using cutting-edge methods in cell and molecular genetics, biochemistry, and functional imaging..." Read twenty of these in your own field and the house style becomes obvious: one specific mechanism, a named unconventional approach, an explicit payoff sentence. That style is the single best proxy available for a winning Pew proposal.

2. SISTER DIRECTORIES, same structure:
- Pew-Stewart: https://www.pew.org/en/projects/pew-stewart-scholars-for-cancer-research/directory-of-stewart-scholars
- Latin American Fellows: https://www.pew.org/en/projects/pew-latin-american-fellows/directory-of-latin-fellows (also lists each fellow's SPONSOR — the practical way to build a target list of US sponsor labs)
- Marine Fellows: https://www.pew.org/en/projects/marine-fellows/fellows-directory

3. ANNUAL PRESS RELEASES — one-paragraph funded-project summaries for a whole class at once, useful for seeing the portfolio's range in a single read. Biomedical scholars announced each June (e.g. "Pew Announces 21 New Biomedical Scholars," June 16, 2026, and the companion article "These 36 Scientists Are Leading the Way to Biomedical Discoveries"). Marine fellows each March ("Pew Awards Fellowships to Seven Scientists Advancing Marine Conservation," March 11, 2026). Innovation Fund each December ("Pew Funds 8 Teams to Conduct Collaborative Biomedical Research," Dec. 10, 2024) — these give paired-investigator project descriptions.

4. THE ORAL HISTORY AND ARCHIVES PROJECT — genuinely unusual and worth knowing about. Launched 1988, it has collected the life stories of more than 200 Pew scholars, "one of the most extensive biomedical research oral history archives available today in the United States." Archived at the Science History Institute in Philadelphia; many are viewable on request. This is where you learn how Pew scholars describe their own risk-taking, which is exactly what the personal statements ask for.

5. TALK TO AWARDEES DIRECTLY — Pew encourages it and will broker it. Scholar profiles publish email addresses. For Latin American Fellows, Pew states outright: "The program's regional committee members are ready and willing to talk with interested candidates. Pew staff can also connect you with current fellows and alumni; email fellowsapp@pewtrusts.org to request an introduction." Also ask your own institution for its past Pew scholars — the Weill Cornell page, for instance, lists its nine past recipients with emails, and Pew advises institutions to put alumni on internal selection committees.

6. INTERNAL INSTITUTIONAL PAGES as a proxy for the application's shape — university limited-submission pages reproduce the pre-proposal prompts that mirror Pew's own: Weill Cornell (https://research.weill.cornell.edu/funding/funding-opportunities/pew-charitable-trusts-pew-biomedical-scholars-program), BU (https://www.bu.edu/research/2026/01/22/the-pew-charitable-trusts-pew-biomedical-scholars-2027/), CU Boulder (https://www.colorado.edu/researchinnovation/pew-biomedical-scholars), Penn State, Dana-Farber/HCC. Treat these as the institution's requirements, not Pew's.

7. GRANT-LEVEL TAX DATA — Pew is a public charity; its IRS Form 990 Schedule I lists grants paid. Available through ProPublica's Nonprofit Explorer and Candid. Useful for amounts and recipient institutions, useless for scientific content. (I did not verify Pew's EIN against an authoritative source, so look it up rather than trusting a third-party aggregator.)

8. ARTS: past grants are browsable at https://www.pewcenterarts.org — "Past Grants" under Our Grantmaking; the Center also publishes evaluative criteria and indicators inside each program's application guidelines, and names its recent panelists. That published-criteria practice is more transparent than the biomedical side.
result.page_limits:
CAUTION ON SOURCING: Pew does not publish its application guide. The guide is emailed only to nominated applicants when the portal opens. The page limits below come from an April 5, 2023 presentation given by Pew's own Project Director, Kara Coleman, Ph.D., to Boston University ("Pew Biomedical Programs Overview," https://www.bu.edu/foundations/files/2024/07/Pew_BU_2023.pdf), describing the 2024 cycle. They are Pew's own numbers but are three cycles old — confirm against the guide you receive on June 10.

PEW SCHOLARS / PEW-STEWART (per that Pew deck):
- Project proposal: "6 pages, double-spaced including figures (limit does not include references)". Note "double-spaced" — this is roughly 3 single-spaced pages of text, far shorter than an R01, and figures count against it while references do not.
- Personal statements: "1 paragraph each" against three prompts (see required_documents). Short.
- CV information: entered as structured portal fields, not uploaded as a document.
- 3 reference letters, submitted by the referees, due two weeks before the deadline.
(The 2023 cycle also had a "COVID impact" field; assume it is gone unless the current guide shows it.)

CROSS-CONFIRMATION THAT THE PROMPTS ARE STILL CURRENT: CU Boulder's 2026/2027-cycle internal page asks for a self-assessment in "Three sections capped at 1,400 characters each covering: significant research, innovative aspects, and personal/scientific background" — the same three prompts, which strongly suggests the personal-statement structure has not drifted. The 6-page proposal limit is the item I would most want re-verified.

PEW LATIN AMERICAN FELLOWS:
- Research proposal: "5 page research proposal *written by the applicant, but work on with sponsor*"
- Personal statements on (a) intent to further a research career in Latin America and (b) most significant scientific contribution during graduate school
- 3 letters of reference, plus — separately — a sponsor letter. Pew is emphatic: "This is separate from the 3 reference letters. The sponsor should not write one of the 3 reference letters listed above."

DO NOT MISTAKE YOUR INSTITUTION'S LIMITS FOR PEW'S. Internal pre-proposal limits for the 2027 cycle vary widely and are set locally, not by Pew: CU Boulder 1 page; BU 2 pages plus one page of references; Weill Cornell 2 pages plus unlimited references, 12-point font, 1-inch margins, plus a 30-line abstract, a 1-2 page chair's nomination letter, a biosketch including the exact first-appointment date, and a 1-page "3 most influential publications" section; Dana-Farber/HCC 1-2 pages plus CV plus chair's letter; Stony Brook 3 pages double-spaced, 12-point Times New Roman, 1-inch margins. The internal application is a different, shorter document than the Pew application.

WHAT VARIES BY MECHANISM: Scholars and Pew-Stewart are identical in machinery and differ only in deadline (Aug. 27 vs Sept. 3), topic (cancer-relevant vs any human-health-relevant), reviewing committee, and pool size (95 cancer centers vs 212 institutions). Latin American Fellows differs substantially: 5-page proposal, sponsor documentation, no institutional nomination, an interview stage. Marine Fellows and the Innovation Fund publish no application specifications at all.

BUDGET RULES THAT SHAPE THE PROPOSAL (Scholars and Pew-Stewart, published): PI salary capped at $12,500/yr including benefits, $50,000 over the grant; no cap on student or postdoc salaries; indirect costs capped at 8 percent ($24,000); no indirect costs on the travel supplement; subawards allowed; carryover allowed; one no-cost extension year available with written approval. Expected effort at least 80 percent on the scholar's overall research goals, but "Pew provides flexible support... and does not require effort reporting."
required_documents: INSTITUTIONAL NOMINATION SURVEY (Scholars / Pew-Stewart) — completed by a member of your institution's internal selection committee, not by you. It describes the selection process the institution used and submits the chosen applicant's name and contact details. Due May 13, 2026; nothing is accepted after that date.

CV INFORMATION — entered as structured fields in the Pew portal rather than uploaded. Must include the exact date of your first assistant professor appointment (month/day/year), education and work history, publications, awards, and all current and pending research support with dollar amounts, dates, and any scientific overlap with the proposed project.
PERSONAL STATEMENT 1 (one paragraph) — 'Briefly describe your most significant research contribution to date.'
PERSONAL STATEMENT 2 (one paragraph) — 'Highlight the most innovative and novel aspects of your proposed research. Describe a risky or creative approach you might use in pursuit of your goals.'

PERSONAL STATEMENT 3 (one paragraph) — 'The program aims to support both the research and the researcher. Please describe how your personal background and past experiences have helped you stand out in your approach to science and your career.'

PROJECT PROPOSAL — 6 pages, double-spaced, figures counted, references excluded (Pew's 2024-cycle specification; re-confirm in the current guide). Pew's guidance: propose a specific project rather than an overall lab vision and say how it fits the lab's broader goals; outline experimental detail even though extensive preliminary data is not required; avoid being purely descriptive; and make it something NOT fundable by traditional mechanisms.

THREE REFERENCE LETTERS — specifically your thesis advisor, your postdoctoral advisor, and a third 'scientific reference.' Submitted by the referees directly, TWO WEEKS BEFORE the application deadline. Pew says the third letter 'is very impactful' and that letters are used to speak to creativity and to your success carrying a project from start to finish.
LATIN AMERICAN FELLOWS — 5-page research proposal, written by the applicant in consultation with the sponsor.

LATIN AMERICAN FELLOWS — written statement of intent to further your research career in Latin America after the fellowship, plus a statement on your most significant scientific contribution during graduate school. (Applicants planning to establish a lab in Cuba or Venezuela must contact the program office first.)

LATIN AMERICAN FELLOWS — three letters of reference from individuals familiar with your work, and SEPARATELY a sponsor letter of commitment to host and train you, the sponsor's CV, and details of the grant funding the sponsoring PI will hold during the award period. The sponsor must not be one of the three referees, and must not be your PhD advisor or mentor.

INTERNAL / PRE-PROPOSAL PACKET (set by your institution, not by Pew, and due months earlier) — typically a 1-3 page research summary, a CV or biosketch showing the first-appointment date, a department chair or division chief letter of support, and sometimes a short abstract, a budget page, or a '3 most influential publications' section. Submitted through your institution's own system (InfoReady, SurveyMonkey Apply, or similar), not through Pew.

PEW CENTER FOR ARTS & HERITAGE (separate funder) — Initial Inquiry Form (no account needed); three years of financial audits or reviews uploaded to the portal's 'My Financials' tab; a Letter of Intent to Apply (Creative Project) or project brief (Evolving Futures); then, if invited, a full application per the published Part II guidelines. Fiscal sponsors must supply their own audits and a sponsorship agreement in place at LOI time.
