result.funder_system:
U.S. Department of Defense (cross-service) — styled "Department of War (DoW)" in FY26/FY27 documents (the FY26 CDMRP announcement writes "the Department of Defense, DOD, herein referred to using the secondary title Department of War, DOW"). Old dod.mil/defense.gov URLs still resolve; war.gov appears for comptroller/budget pages.

CRITICAL FRAMING FOR APPLICANTS: "DoD" is not one funder system. It is FOUR machineries that share only SAM.gov registration. Nothing else transfers between them, and the most common first-timer error is applying NIH habits to the wrong one.

TRACK 1 — SERVICE BASIC RESEARCH (ARO/ARL, ONR, AFOSR; plus DARPA). This is where a PhD-holding academic goes. Mechanism = Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) / Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO). Canonical path is: TALK TO A PROGRAM OFFICER -> WHITE PAPER -> INVITED FULL PROPOSAL. Rolling or annual. No study section; program officers and internal panels decide.

TRACK 2 — CDMRP (Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs), under Defense Health Agency R&D. Biomedical. This is the NIH-lookalike: two-tier peer review, summary statements, consumer reviewers, fixed annual deadlines. But it is the OPPOSITE of NIH on program-officer contact (see program_officer_norms). FY26 PRMRP appropriation alone was $370M; PRMRP FY99-FY25 totals $4.34 billion.

TRACK 3 — SBIR/STTR. Small-business-led; STTR requires a research-institution partner, so this is how a university lab gets in. Monthly release cycle, contract-style, own portal (DSIP).

TRACK 4 — FELLOWSHIPS AND INSTRUMENTATION for the individual/institution: NDSEG (PhD students), YIP (ECR faculty), DURIP (equipment), Vannevar Bush Faculty Fellowship (senior), DEPSCoR, HBCU/MI. Mostly annual with published dates.

CAREER-STAGE LADDER (the practical answer to "what can I apply for"):
- PhD student, US citizen/national/dual, >=3 years remaining: NDSEG Fellowship (you apply yourself, no institution needed).
- Postdoc: no direct DoD postdoc grant on the academic track; route in as named personnel on a PI's BAA award, via NRC Research Associateship at a service lab, or as the research-institution partner on an STTR.
- ECR faculty, first/second full-time tenure-track position, PhD within ~7-8 years, US citizen/national/permanent resident: ONR YIP, AFOSR YIP, ARO Early Career Program (ECP). These are the flagship DoD ECR awards. NOTE the hard eligibility walls: ONR YIP bars tenured faculty, bars co-PIs, bars prior YIP recipients.
- Any faculty stage: the open service BAAs (AFOSR FA955026S0001, ARL W911NF-23-S-0001, ONR Long Range BAA) — these accept unsolicited proposals year-round and are the single most under-used DoD entry point for academics.
- Team/multi-institution: MURI (tri-service, ~$1.5M/yr for 5 yrs).
- Equipment only: DURIP ($50k-$3M; buys instruments, NOT salaries or research costs).
result.submission_portal:
There is no single DoD portal. Which one you use is determined by the track, and the account setup is the hidden long-lead item.

1) SAM.gov — THE UNIVERSAL PREREQUISITE. Generates the Unique Entity ID (UEI). Your institution must hold "Active" status BEFORE submission and must renew annually. CDMRP FY26 announcement, verbatim: "Active SAM.gov, eBRAP.org and Grants.gov registrations are required for application submission. User registration for each of these websites can take several weeks or longer." Also: the organization must "maintain an active registration in the SAM at all times during which it has an active Federal award or an application under consideration." A lapsed institutional SAM registration silently kills a submission. Check with your research office 6-8 weeks out — you cannot fix this yourself.

2) Grants.gov (grants and cooperative agreements to universities) — used by ARO, ONR, AFOSR, CDMRP extramural, MURI, DURIP, YIP, DEPSCoR. Only the institution's Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR) can press submit; a PI cannot. Grants.gov VALIDATION is separate from receipt and can take up to 48 hours. FY26 MURI NOFO: "Applications must be 'VALIDATED' by Grants.gov by the application deadline, which can take up to 48 hours after successful submission... It is strongly recommended that applications be submitted at least 2 business days ahead of the stated deadline." After submitting you get THREE emails; ONR states you have only reached the agency when email #3 arrives. Note grants.gov's new front end is simpler.grants.gov, which renders reliably; legacy grants.gov detail URLs often return an empty shell to a plain fetch.

3) eBRAP (ebrap.org) — CDMRP only. A MANDATORY PRE-APPLICATION step in eBRAP precedes every CDMRP mechanism: "Pre-application submission to eBRAP by the pre-application submission deadline is mandatory for all award mechanisms." Extramural organizations then submit the FULL application through Grants.gov; only intramural DoD organizations submit full applications in eBRAP. The eBRAP Application Log Number must be entered in the Grants.gov package (SF424 R&R Block 4a "Federal Identifier" / "Application Filing Name"). PI, Business Official and AOR all register separately and an organizational affiliation must be APPROVED by email before you can work on a full application. Pre-application left in "DRAFT" after the deadline = ineligible to submit at all, no grace period.

4) SAM.gov Contract Opportunities — DARPA office-wide BAAs and many ARL/service contract BAAs are posted here, NOT on grants.gov, because they award contracts and Other Transactions rather than grants. DARPA's own BAA page says office-wide BAAs "are refreshed annually" and points to sam.gov. First-timers routinely miss DARPA entirely by only watching grants.gov.

5) DARPA BAAT — baa.darpa.mil. "DARPA encourages proposers to submit UNCLASSIFIED proposals via DARPA's Broad Agency Announcement Tool (BAAT)." Uploads must be zip archives (.zip/.zipx), max 100 MB. "Email submissions will not be accepted."

6) DSIP — dodsbirsttr.mil, the Defense SBIR/STTR Innovation Portal. SBIR/STTR only. Three separate registrations, all slow: (a) SAM.gov; (b) SBA Company Registry — "SBCs should start registration process early as verification cannot be expedited and a valid SBC Control ID is required for proposal submission in DSIP"; (c) individual DSIP user accounts authenticated by Login.gov, with a designated Firm Admin who creates the Firm PIN. HARD GOTCHA: "The DSIP application is only accessible from within the United States" — you cannot submit while travelling abroad.

7) FedConnect — ONR white papers (contract-side) go here, not grants.gov. ONR warns: "Do NOT use the FedConnect message center to submit questions or responses to this announcement. The message center is not monitored."

8) APAN community portal — AFOSR white papers: https://community.apan.org/wg/afosr/p/submitawhitepaper

9) ndseg.sysplus.com — NDSEG fellowship, applied for directly by the student.

REALISTIC LEAD TIME: 6-8 weeks before your first DoD submission, start SAM/eBRAP/Grants.gov/DSIP registration. This is the single most common cause of a missed DoD deadline and it is entirely administrative.
result.deadline_structure:
Four coexisting structures. Real published dates follow (all verified from funder documents or the grants.gov listing, dated as of 18 Sep 2026).

A) ROLLING / CONTINUOUSLY OPEN BAAs — the big under-used door. No deadline; you submit when your program officer says the white paper is ready.
- AFOSR "Research Interests of the Air Force Office of Scientific Research", FA955026S0001 — posted 4 Jun 2026, closes 31 Aug 2029 (grants.gov listing). Predecessor FA955025S0001 was closed early, verbatim: "Broad Agency Announcement FA955025S0001 is closed as of 23 March 2026 due to a new mandatory review process, as required by Executive Order 14332."
- DEVCOM ARL BAA for Foundational Research, W911NF-23-S-0001 — posted 21 Nov 2022, closes 20 Nov 2027, ~2,000 expected awards (grants.gov listing).
- ONR Long Range BAA — verbatim: "This announcement will remain open for approximately one (1) year from the date of publication, or until replaced by a successor BAA. Proposals may be submitted at any time during this period." Refreshed roughly each 1 October. FY25 edition N0001425SB001 (published 1 Oct 2024) accepted full proposals until 30 Sep 2026 2:00 PM EST. An FY27 successor is expected but I could not locate it (see unresolved).

B) ANNUAL NAMED COMPETITIONS — dates published each cycle. Currently open or recently closed, with real dates:
- ONR FY2027 Young Investigator Program, N0001426SF004: questions 16 Oct 2026; PROPOSALS DUE 30 Oct 2026 5:00 PM ET; notification of selection 16 Feb 2027; grant start 1 Apr 2027. "IMPORTANT NOTE: White Papers are NOT being solicited and will NOT be accepted."
- AFOSR FY2027 YIP, FA955026S0003: posted 8 Sep 2026, closes 4 Dec 2026 (grants.gov listing).
- FY2027 DURIP (tri-service ARO/ONR/AFOSR): pre-proposal inquiries 16 Oct 2026; proposals due 6 Nov 2026 5:00 PM ET. AFOSR number NOFOAFRLAFOSR20260001 (posted 29 Jul 2026, closes 6 Nov 2026).
- AFOSR FY26 DEPSCoR Research Collaboration (NOFOAFRLAFOSR20260004) and Capacity Building (NOFOAFRLAFOSR20260003): both posted 10 Aug 2026, close 5 Apr 2027.
- ONR FY2027 HBCU/MI, N0001426SF001: due 11 Dec 2026.
- NDSEG FY2027 cycle: "August 3 at 12:01 AM – October 30 at 5 PM Eastern" (2026).
- FY26 MURI (tri-service ONR N0001425SF002 / ARO W911NF25S0004 / AFOSR NOFOAFRLAFOSR20250002), as the FULL ANNUAL SHAPE to plan against: white paper inquiries 18 Apr 2025; WHITE PAPERS DUE 2 May 2025 5:00 PM ET; white-paper feedback 13 Jun 2025; proposal questions 22 Aug 2025; FULL PROPOSALS DUE 5 Sep 2025 5:00 PM ET; notification of selection Jan 2026; grant start 1 May 2026. Pattern to expect annually: white paper ~April/May, proposal ~September, award ~May.

C) CDMRP — per-fiscal-year announcement, TWO deadlines about two weeks apart. Actual FY26 PRMRP Discovery Award (HT942526PRMRPDA): "Pre-Application (Letter of Intent) Submission Deadline: 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time (ET), July 16, 2026"; "Application Submission Deadline: 11:59 p.m. ET, July 30, 2026"; "End of Application Verification Period: 5:00 p.m. ET, August 5, 2026"; "Peer Review: September/October 2026"; "Programmatic Review: December 2026/January 2027". CDMRP announcements typically post spring/early summer for a summer deadline; there is no NIH-style standing calendar of recurring dates — you must watch grants.gov Assistance Listing 12.420 and subscribe to eBRAP email alerts. Verbatim: "There are no grace periods for deadlines; failure to meet submission deadlines will result in application rejection."

D) SBIR/STTR — MONTHLY, the most regular calendar DoD publishes. New topics pre-release the FIRST WEDNESDAY of each month; open ~3 weeks later; close ~4 weeks after opening at 12:00 p.m. ET. FY2026 SBIR BAA matrix, verbatim:
Release 1: pre-release 13 Apr 2026, open 6 May 2026, close 3 Jun 2026
Release 2: pre-release 6 May 2026, open 27 May 2026, close 24 Jun 2026
Release 3: pre-release 3 Jun 2026, open 24 Jun 2026, close 22 Jul 2026
Release 4: pre-release 1 Jul 2026, open 22 Jul 2026, close 19 Aug 2026
Release 5: pre-release 5 Aug 2026, open 26 Aug 2026, close 23 Sep 2026
Release 6: pre-release 2 Sep 2026, open 23 Sep 2026, close 21 Oct 2026
"UNLESS OTHERWISE STATED WITHIN THE TOPIC, complete proposals must be certified and submitted in DSIP no later than 12:00p.m. ET on the close date." Note NOON, not midnight — this catches people.

A NOTE ON DATES AND DRIFT (relevant to whether dated deadlines belong in this corpus): dates here are load-bearing and were verified against funder PDFs, but they are the fastest-rotting fact in the corpus. Three live examples of why the date must always carry its cycle label and source: (i) the AFOSR open BAA was killed mid-cycle by EO 14332; (ii) the FY26 MURI NOFO contradicts itself internally — the cover page says proposals due 5 Sep 2025 while Section F.1 says "All applications must be received by 5:00 PM Eastern Time on 22 AUGUST 2025"; (iii) ONR's Long Range BAA deadline moves every October. The safe pattern for a user-facing interface is to publish the RECURRING SHAPE (white paper April, proposal September, award May) as the durable fact, and the specific date as a dated, sourced, expiring annotation.

review_stages.stage: TRACK 1 (service BAA) — Step 0: Program officer conversation. Not a formal stage but functionally gating. Email the PO/Topic Chief/TPOC with a short topic description; they tell you whether to proceed.
review_stages.timing: Anytime; for an annual competition, 2-4 months before the white paper deadline. ONR: 'Please allow adequate time for such discussions with the ONR Program Officer.'

review_stages.stage: TRACK 1 — White paper submitted (4-5 pages). ARL's recommended sequence verbatim: 'Conduct a preliminary inquiry with an ARL TPOC; Submit a Whitepaper to an ARL TPOC for review; Submit a Full Proposal.'
review_stages.timing: Month 0. MURI FY26: 2 May 2025. AFOSR YIP FY26: 25 Jul 2025.

review_stages.stage: TRACK 1 — White paper feedback: the Topic Chief gives informal encourage/discourage. MURI verbatim: 'the responsible Research Topic Chief will provide informal feedback notification to the prospective awardees to encourage or discourage submission of proposals. The Research Topic Chief may also, on occasion, provide feedback encouraging re-teaming to strengthen a proposal.' This is NOT a selection; AFOSR: 'White paper evaluation is meant to initially assess the capability of a proposed effort and is NOT a selection process.'
review_stages.timing: ~6 weeks after white paper. MURI FY26: 13 Jun 2025 (WP due 2 May). AFOSR YIP FY26: response by 22 Aug 2025 (WP due 25 Jul).

review_stages.stage: TRACK 1 — Full proposal via Grants.gov (or BAAT/SAM.gov for contracts). Grants.gov validation up to 48h.
review_stages.timing: ~4 months after white paper. MURI FY26: 5 Sep 2025. AFOSR YIP FY26: 19 Sep 2025. ONR YIP FY27: 30 Oct 2026.

review_stages.stage: TRACK 1 — Evaluation. NO external study section and NO public roster. MURI verbatim: 'The ultimate recommendation for award of proposals is made by the DoD's scientific/technical community.' AFOSR YIP: 'We will evaluate proposals using an internal review panel.' DARPA: 'DARPA will conduct a scientific/technical review of each conforming proposal.' There is no council/advisory-board second step equivalent to NIH Council.
review_stages.timing: 3-5 months. No summary statement is produced on this track — feedback, if any, comes informally from the PO.

review_stages.stage: TRACK 1 — Notification of selection. Recommendation is not an award: MURI warns a recommendation 'does not guarantee an award will ultimately be made' and is 'sent to the Grants Department to conduct cost analysis, determine the Applicant's responsibility, to confirm whether funds are available.'
review_stages.timing: ~4-5 months after proposal. MURI FY26: Jan 2026 (proposal 5 Sep 2025). AFOSR YIP FY26: 'no later than 14 February 2026.' ONR YIP FY27: 16 Feb 2027.

review_stages.stage: TRACK 1 — Negotiation with the Grants Officer, then award start. Only a warranted Grants/Contracting Officer can obligate funds.
review_stages.timing: ~2-4 months after notification. MURI FY26 start: 1 May 2026 (12 months after white paper, 8 after proposal). AFOSR YIP FY26 awards 'by 01 March 2026.' ONR YIP FY27 start: 1 Apr 2027.

review_stages.stage: TRACK 2 (CDMRP) — Pre-application (LOI or pre-proposal) in eBRAP. Screened only for compliance and conflict of interest, not science. LOI = no gate, proceed; pre-proposal = invite/not-invite gate. FY26 PRMRP Discovery: 'There is no review and selection process for pre-applications... CDMRP will NOT provide an invitation.'
review_stages.timing: Month 0. FY26 PRMRP Discovery: 16 Jul 2026.

review_stages.stage: TRACK 2 — Full application via Grants.gov (extramural) or eBRAP (intramural), then a VERIFICATION PERIOD in eBRAP during which you confirm what was received. This step has no NIH analogue and is easy to miss.
review_stages.timing: ~2 weeks after pre-app; verification closes ~1 week later. FY26: application 30 Jul 2026, verification ends 5 Aug 2026.

review_stages.stage: TRACK 2 — TIER 1 PEER REVIEW. Panels of 'scientists, clinicians, consumers, and specialists'. 'All CDMRP peer review panels include consumer reviewers' — a survivor/patient/caregiver sits on the panel and scores your application, which is the single biggest writing difference from NIH (hence the mandatory one-page Lay Abstract). Scores: overall merit 1-5 (1 best), individual criteria 1-10. Produces a written Summary Statement.
review_stages.timing: 2 months after the application deadline, sometimes 3. FY26 PRMRP Discovery: 'Peer Review: September/October 2026.'

review_stages.stage: TRACK 2 — TIER 2 PROGRAMMATIC REVIEW. A separate multidisciplinary panel of 'consumers, clinicians, laboratory scientists, and other key stakeholders' compares high-scoring applications for portfolio fit; they see 'the Summary Statement, the Abstract, and selected attachments', not the full application. Verbatim warning: 'The highest-scoring applications from the first tier of review are not automatically recommended for funding.' This is the closest DoD equivalent to NIH Council but it is a portfolio-balance step, not a rubber stamp.
review_stages.timing: ~5 months after the application deadline. FY26 PRMRP Discovery: 'Programmatic Review: December 2026/January 2027.'

review_stages.stage: TRACK 2 — Notification + Summary Statement posted to eBRAP. Everyone gets the summary statement; non-funded applicants also get a brief statement of the primary reason for non-selection.
review_stages.timing: 'typically within 6 weeks after programmatic review' (FY26 announcement); CDMRP's process page says 'approximately three-to-six weeks', with January programmatic review meaning notification 'by mid-March, if not earlier'. So ~6-7 months from the application deadline.

review_stages.stage: TRACK 2 — Grants Officer negotiation and award. 'Only an appointed DHACA Grants Officer may obligate the government.' You may incur costs up to 90 days pre-award at your own risk.
review_stages.timing: FY26 funds: 'Awards supported with FY26 funds will be made no later than September 30, 2027' — i.e. up to 14 months after the 30 Jul 2026 deadline.

review_stages.stage: TRACK 3 (SBIR/STTR) — Topic pre-release (direct TPOC contact allowed) -> topics open -> Topic Q&A closes 2 weeks before close -> proposal certified and submitted in DSIP by 12:00 noon ET.
review_stages.timing: Pre-release to close is ~10 weeks total (e.g. Release 5: 5 Aug -> 26 Aug -> Q&A closes 9 Sep -> closes 23 Sep 2026).

review_stages.stage: TRACK 3 — Component evaluation and selection, then contract negotiation. Handled per Service/Component, not centrally; DSIP Support explicitly 'cannot provide updates to proposal status after submission.'
review_stages.timing: Varies by component; commonly ~3-6 months from close to Phase I award. NOT ESTABLISHED from a primary cross-service source — treat as approximate.

result.months_submission_to_award:
Depends entirely on track. Measured from the deadline you actually submit to:

TRACK 1, service BAA annual competitions — 5 to 8 months to award start; 12 months if you count from the white paper.
- MURI FY26: white paper 2 May 2025 -> proposal 5 Sep 2025 -> selection Jan 2026 -> START 1 May 2026. = 4 months proposal-to-notification, 8 months proposal-to-start, 12 months white-paper-to-start.
- AFOSR YIP FY26: white paper 25 Jul 2025 -> proposal 19 Sep 2025 -> notification by 14 Feb 2026 -> awards by 1 Mar 2026. = ~5 months proposal-to-notification, ~5.5 to award.
- ONR YIP FY27: proposal 30 Oct 2026 -> notification 16 Feb 2027 -> start 1 Apr 2027. = 3.5 months to notification, 5 months to start.

TRACK 1, rolling open BAAs — no fixed clock. Practically, plan 6-12 months from first PO email to money, and expect the PO to tell you which fiscal year they are buying against. A rolling BAA does not mean rolling money: service budgets are annual, so a PO may ask you to submit at a particular time to hit a funding line.

TRACK 2, CDMRP — 6 to 7 months from the application deadline to notification + summary statement; up to 14 months to award obligation. FY26 PRMRP Discovery: application 30 Jul 2026 -> peer review Sep/Oct 2026 -> programmatic Dec 2026/Jan 2027 -> notification ~Feb/Mar 2027 -> "Awards supported with FY26 funds will be made no later than September 30, 2027."

TRACK 3, SBIR/STTR — ~2.5 months pre-release to close; Phase I award typically a further ~3-6 months (approximate; not established from a primary cross-service document).

TRACK 4, NDSEG — cycle closes 30 Oct 2026 for a fellowship whose tenure starts the following fall, so ~10 months application-to-start.

PLANNING RULE OF THUMB for a PhD student / postdoc / ECR: a DoD academic award will not pay salary until roughly one year after you first email the program officer. Budget for that gap; do not treat DoD as a bridge for a funding cliff less than 12 months away.
result.resubmission_policy:
There is NO DoD-wide A0/A1 resubmission machinery. NIH habits actively mislead here, in both directions.

CDMRP — no formal resubmission mechanism exists. An unfunded application is not "revised and resubmitted"; you write a fresh application to a future funding opportunity and it is reviewed as new, with no reference to the prior submission and no reviewer awareness of it. There is therefore NO introduction page, NO response-to-reviewers section, and no limit on how many times you may try, beyond per-cycle limits. The FY26 PRMRP announcement enforces a one-application-per-PI rule within the cycle: "Each investigator may be named on only one FY26 PRMRP application as PI. If more than one pre-application submitted to the FY26 PRMRP names the same PI, the first submission will be accepted, and subsequent submissions will be administratively withdrawn." Practically you still get the most valuable resubmission input NIH offers — CDMRP gives EVERY applicant a full peer review Summary Statement with scored criteria, strengths and weaknesses, plus a brief statement of the primary reason for non-selection. Mine it and rewrite for the next fiscal year's announcement, which may have different topic areas and strategic goals.

CDMRP APPEALS — there is an Inquiry Review Process (IRP), and it is narrow. Verbatim: "If an application is not recommended for funding and the applicant believes a factual or procedural error occurred during the review of the application, the organization or PI may submit an inquiry through the eBRAP Help Desk at help@eBRAP.org within 15 business days after the notification letter is sent. Inquiries submitted after 15 business days will not be considered." Only factual or procedural error counts: "Differences of opinion between reviewers or between reviewer(s) and an applicant are not factual errors." And: "Inquiries that provide a point-by-point rebuttal to multiple weaknesses in the summary statement without clearly identifying and addressing specific perceived factual or procedural error(s) in the review will not be considered." Also: "The determination of an error in the review process is not a guarantee of re-review or funding." Do not use the IRP as a disguised rebuttal — it is for "you left my Letter of Support out of the review package", not "the reviewer was wrong about my controls".

SERVICE BAAs (ARO/ONR/AFOSR/DARPA) — the concept does not exist. There is no resubmission marking, no introduction page, no counted attempts. A declined white paper or proposal is simply re-pitched to the program officer, revised, and submitted again — often to the same rolling BAA, sometimes within the same year. The PO is the gate, so the real "resubmission strategy" is a conversation: ask the PO why it did not get funded and whether the topic is still live. MURI's Grants.gov guidance uses "resubmission" only in the clerical sense of a package that failed the automated check: "Block 2, 'Type of Application' on the SF-424 should be marked 'New' on the resubmission" — i.e. even a re-sent package is marked New, never Resubmission.

HARD BARS THAT ARE NOT RESUBMISSION LIMITS BUT FUNCTION AS ONE — read these before planning a second attempt. ONR YIP FY27: "This is a single PI award. Co-PIs are not allowed. Tenured faculty are ineligible to apply. Prior ONR YIP Award recipients are ineligible to apply." YIP eligibility is also a rolling PhD-date window (ONR FY27: PhD "on or after 01/01/2019"; AFOSR FY26: "01 April 2018 or later"), so for ECRs the number of attempts is bounded by the clock, not by policy — count your remaining eligible years and plan two or three shots, not one.

SBIR/STTR — you resubmit to a later monthly release. Note that "Once the proposal submission closes, no communication of any kind is allowed either with the topic author or through topic Q&A regarding submitted proposals," so there is no debrief route until the component's own post-award debrief process.

ONE-OFF, WORTH KNOWING AS A PATTERN: when AFOSR's open BAA was terminated mid-cycle under Executive Order 14332, proposals submitted 18-23 Mar 2026 "must be resubmitted to the upcoming Open BAA." A DoD solicitation can be withdrawn under you and your submission voided; keep your submitted package and confirmation emails so you can re-lodge quickly.
result.page_limits:
DoD page limits are SHORT compared to NIH — a 4-page CDMRP narrative or a 4-5 page white paper is the norm — and the standard set varies more by mechanism than at NIH. Verified limits:

CDMRP (FY26 PRMRP Discovery Award, HT942526PRMRPDA — mechanism-specific, so check your own announcement):
- Letter of Intent / pre-application: 1 page
- Attachment 1 Project Narrative: 4 pages ("four-page limit") — and for this mechanism, "Applications must not include preliminary data... The presentation of preliminary and/or published data is not allowed and may result in administrative withdrawal."
- Attachment 3 Technical Abstract: 1 page
- Attachment 4 Lay Abstract: 1 page (written for the consumer reviewers)
- Attachment 5 Statement of Work: 3 pages
- Attachment 6 Innovation Statement: 1 page
- Attachment 7 Impact Statement: 1 page
- Attachment 8 Relevance to Military Health Statement: 1 page
- Attachment 9 Animal Research Plan: 3 pages (if applicable)
- Sex as a Biological Variable Strategy: 2 pages
- DoD Data Management Plan: "no more than two pages"
- Supporting Documentation, References Cited, biosketches, current/pending: "There are no page limits for these components unless otherwise noted", but material used as "an extension of the Project Narrative will result in the removal of those items."
CDMRP is brutal about this: exceeding the Project Narrative page limit causes ADMINISTRATIVE REJECTION, not truncation. Other over-length attachments are trimmed: "Pages exceeding the specified limits will be removed prior to reviewing all documents. Documents not requested will be removed."

CDMRP UNIVERSAL FORMATTING (General Application Instructions Appendix 2, identical across all CDMRP mechanisms): 12-point Times New Roman, not condensed; single-spaced or no more than six lines per vertical inch; page no larger than 8.5 x 11 in; margins at least 0.5 in; print area 7.5 x 10 in; scanning 100-150 dpi; JPEG only for images (bitmap and TIFF not allowed); NO headers or footers; NO page numbering; NO URLs in the application ("Inclusion of such URLs may be perceived as an attempt to gain an unfair competitive advantage", though "links to publications referenced in the application are encouraged"); English only; individual attachments should be under 20 MB and the whole Grants.gov package may not exceed 200 MB. One trap: "All contributors to the application must use matching compatible versions of Adobe software... The use of different software versions will result in corruption of the submitted file."

SERVICE BAA / NOFO (ARO, ONR, AFOSR, MURI):
- White paper: 4 pages (MURI, "excluding cover letter, cover page, references, and curriculum vitae"; "White paper pages beyond the 4-page limit may not be evaluated or read") or 5 pages (AFOSR YIP, "References and CV/bios will not count"; ONR Long Range BAA, "5 pages (excluding cover page)").
- Full technical proposal: 20-25 pages. MURI: 25 pages, counting only Technical Approach/Project Narrative, Management Approach, and PI Qualifications — "Everything else" is excluded. AFOSR YIP: "No more than twenty (20) single-sided pages." ONR YIP FY27: 20 pages, excluding cover page, table of contents, full CV, data management plan, letters of support, cited references, current and pending support. "There are no page limitations for the budget."
- Universal BAA formatting: 8.5 x 11 in, 1-inch margins, single-spaced, Times New Roman 12-point. Filename rule that silently breaks submissions: "The electronic file name for all documents submitted under this NOFO must not exceed 68 characters in length, including the file name extension."
- CV limit where stated: MURI, "limited to 5 pages per CV".

SBIR/STTR (DSIP): Technical Volume (Volume 2) is a single PDF, no type smaller than 10-point, 8.5 x 11 in, one-inch margins including the header, pages numbered consecutively, header on every page carrying firm name, topic number and DSIP proposal number. Page COUNT is set per Service/Component, not centrally — and "Some Services/Components will reject the entire technical proposal if the proposal exceeds the stated page count." No locked/password-protected/encrypted files; no embedded video.

DARPA: proposals uploaded to BAAT as .zip/.zipx, max 100 MB; page limits are set per individual BAA.
required_documents: SF-424 Research & Related (R&R) Application for Federal Assistance — the cover form for every Grants.gov submission. AFOSR: 'The SF 424 (R&R) ... must be your cover page. No pages may precede the SF 424 (R&R).' For CDMRP: 'enter the eBRAP log number assigned during pre-application submission into Block 4a - Federal Identifier.' For ONR YIP, a Program Officer Code identifier must be supplied or the proposal is flagged.
R&R Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded), with a Biographical Sketch for each senior/key person (MURI: CV limited to 5 pages)

Current & Pending Support / Current and Pending (Other) Support for every covered individual — no page limit, and legally serious. MURI: disclosure is required under Section 223 of the FY21 NDAA, and 'Failure to report fully and completely all sources of project support and outside positions and affiliations may be considered a materials statement within the meaning of the federal False Claims Act.'
R&R Budget and budget justification (no page limit on either track)
R&R Subaward Budget Attachment(s) — Grants.gov submissions only, if you have subawards
Project/Performance Site Location(s) form
Technical Proposal / Project Narrative — the scored body (CDMRP 4 pp for Discovery; MURI 25 pp; AFOSR YIP 20 pp; ONR YIP 20 pp)

Data Management Plan — REQUIRED DoD-wide and distinct from NIH's. CDMRP: 'a data management plan compliant with Section 3.c, Enclosure 3, DoD Instructions 3200.12', max 2 pages, and explicitly 'applicants should not simply upload a copy of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Data Management and Sharing Plan.' AFOSR requires one modelled on the NSF DMP requirement. Do not recycle your NIH DMSP.
Statement of Work (SOW) — CDMRP 3 pp, with a suggested format template downloadable from eBRAP; standard on the BAA side too

Foreign affiliation / foreign-influence disclosure for all key personnel. CDMRP: 'In accordance with National Security Presidential Memorandum-33 ... All applicant organizations must disclose foreign affiliations of all key personnel named on applications. Failure to disclose foreign affiliations of key personnel shall lead to withdrawal of recommendations to fund applications.' Expect this on every DoD track; it has no NIH equivalent in strictness and is the most common cause of a late-stage DoD award falling over.

Conflict of Interest / Conflict of Commitment disclosure — a pre-award COI/COC review may be run 'as described in the DoD Component Decision Matrix to Inform Fundamental Research Proposal Mitigation Decisions', and 'any significant conflict of interest/conflict of commitment identified may be a basis for the rejection of an otherwise awardable proposal'

Letters of Support where required — MECHANISM-CRITICAL for some: ONR YIP FY27 states an applicant 'MUST submit a research proposal and at least one Letter of Support through the appropriate university officials. Applications received without at least one letter of support will be considered incomplete and will not be considered for award.' Conversely CDMRP strips unrequested letters: 'Letters of support not requested in the program announcement, such as those from members of Congress, will be removed from the application package.'

CDMRP-SPECIFIC ADDITIONAL ATTACHMENTS, each a separately named PDF with a prescribed filename (ProjectNarrative.pdf, TechAbs.pdf, LayAbs.pdf, SOW.pdf, Innovation.pdf, Impact.pdf, Support.pdf etc.): Technical Abstract, LAY ABSTRACT (for consumer reviewers — no DoD-outside analogue), Innovation Statement, Impact Statement, RELEVANCE TO MILITARY HEALTH STATEMENT (the make-or-break section for a first-timer; a scientifically excellent application with a weak military-relevance case does not clear programmatic review), Sex as a Biological Variable Strategy, Animal Research Plan, References Cited

SBIR/STTR (DSIP) volumes: Volume 1 Proposal Cover Sheet (prepared in DSIP), Volume 2 Technical Volume, Volume 3 Cost Volume (DSIP form), Volume 4 Company Commercialization Report (downloaded from SBIR.gov and uploaded to DSIP 'Firm Forms' by the Firm Admin), plus firm-level certifications, SBA Company Registry proof of registration and SBC Control ID, and percentage-of-work certification
DARPA: proposal package as a single .zip/.zipx to BAAT, max 100 MB; contents per the individual BAA
result.program_officer_norms:
This is where DoD differs most from every other funder and where the two internal tracks contradict each other. Get this wrong and you either waste a year or get your application withdrawn.

=== TRACK 1 (SERVICE BASIC RESEARCH: ARO/ARL, ONR, AFOSR, DARPA): CONTACT IS EXPECTED, AND EFFECTIVELY MANDATORY ===
Stronger than NIH. The program officer is not an adviser on the side; they are the decision-maker, and on the rolling BAAs a proposal that arrives without a prior conversation usually goes nowhere.

Verbatim evidence:
- ONR YIP FY27: "Applicants are STRONGLY ENCOURAGED to contact the appropriate Program Officer who is the point of contact for a specific technical area to discuss their research ideas before submitting a proposal... Such discussions can clarify the content and breadth of the priority research areas and enhance the match between a subsequent proposal and Department of the Navy research needs. Please allow adequate time for such discussions with the ONR Program Officer." Mechanics: email a brief topic description to the PO, cc ONRYIP@navy.mil on the first email only.
- ONR Long Range BAA: "White Papers are frequently desired by ONR Program Officers. Offerors should consult the cognizant ONR Program Officer for each technology area regarding the desirability of White Paper submissions." The PO's name and email are MANDATORY FIELDS on the white paper cover page: "FedConnect will not accept a white paper unless the Cover Page is included."
- AFOSR YIP FY26: "Proposers are encouraged to confer with the designated AFOSR Program Officer(s) prior to submitting a full proposal." And on the open BAA: "The AFOSR open BAA updates annually in the March/April time frame. Please make sure you coordinate your topic ideas with the appropriate Program Officer (PO) to ensure the topic area is still relevant to the Air Force."
- DEVCOM ARL: "To conserve valuable applicant and Government resources, interested applicants are strongly encouraged to make a preliminary inquiry by first contacting the ARL TPOC to discuss your ideas," with the recommended sequence "preliminary inquiry -> whitepaper -> full proposal."
- MURI FY26: PIs contemplating appearing on more than one topic "are strongly encouraged to contact the Topic Chief(s) prior to white paper submission."
- DARPA: the program manager defines the program and selects performers; the abstract stage exists precisely so the PM can "encourage or discourage" a full proposal, and Proposers' Days are the designated venue.

WHEN: for a rolling BAA, any time — but at least 3-6 months before you want money, and preferably before you write anything. For an annual competition, 2-4 months before the white paper deadline. Note DoD fiscal rhythm: POs are busiest and least able to commit in August-September (end of fiscal year); the productive window is roughly October-March.

WHAT EXPERIENCED APPLICANTS ACTUALLY ASK (all legitimate and normal on this track):
- "Is this topic still a priority for you, or has the portfolio moved?" — the highest-value question, because rolling BAAs list topics that a PO may have quietly stopped funding.
- "Whose problem does this solve on the DoD side?" — i.e. the transition story. DoD funds basic research, but a PO must justify it against a capability need.
- "Do you want a white paper, and by when to hit your funding line?" — POs work to obligation deadlines and will often tell you the month.
- "Is the size right?" — typical award sizes (AFOSR core: roughly $100k-$300k/yr, usually 3 years; ONR YIP $750k/3yr; AFOSR YIP $450k/3yr; MURI ~$1.5M/yr for 5 years).
- "Should this go to you or to a colleague?" — POs routinely redirect to the right division, which is worth an email on its own.
- "Am I eligible?" — especially YIP tenure-track-equivalent and PhD-date rules.
DO NOT ask them to review a draft proposal, or to predict whether you will be funded.

=== TRACK 2 (CDMRP): CONTACT IS STRUCTURALLY ABSENT AND PARTLY PROHIBITED ===
The exact opposite, inside the same department. CDMRP publishes NO program-manager contact route for applicants. The General Application Instructions list only two "Agency Contacts": the eBRAP Help Desk (help@eBRAP.org, 301-682-5507, M-F 8am-5pm ET) for "Questions related to program announcement content or submission requirements", and the Grants.gov Contact Center for portal problems. Note "The eBRAP Help Desk will not provide Grants.gov submission assistance" — the two help desks each disclaim the other's territory, so ask the right one.

And approaching the review chain is an administrative-withdrawal offence. FY26 PRMRP Discovery, verbatim, among the grounds for withdrawal: "Personnel from applicant or collaborating organizations are found to have contacted persons involved in the review or approval process to gain protected evaluation information or to influence the evaluation process." Also withdrawn if "A member of the FY26 PRMRP Programmatic Panel is named as being involved in the development or execution of the research proposed or is found to have assisted in the pre-application or application processes" — so check the published Programmatic Panel roster on the CDMRP website BEFORE you recruit collaborators or request letters, because a panel member on your team voids the application.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD ON CDMRP: (1) read the funding opportunity end-to-end before writing — the announcement tells you to; (2) use the eBRAP Help Desk aggressively and early for compliance questions, quoting the program announcement version code (e.g. CD26_01d) — this is normal and expected; (3) use the CDMRP video series, application-process FAQ and the Guide for Intragovernmental & Intramural Applicants; (4) get your programmatic fit from the published topic areas, strategic goals and prior funded abstracts rather than from a person; (5) talk to a consumer advocate in your disease area about the Lay Abstract.

=== TRACK 3 (SBIR/STTR): A NARROW, TIME-BOXED WINDOW ===
Unique and precisely regulated. Three phases:
- DURING PRE-RELEASE ONLY: "the names of the topic authors, their phone numbers and/or email addresses are published with the topic... proposing SBCs can contact topic authors via telephone or email to ask technical questions." But: "Questions must be limited to specific information related to understanding a particular topic's requirements. Proposing SBCs may not ask for advice or guidance on solution approach and may not submit additional material to the topic author." Anything material said to you gets published to everyone: "If information provided during an exchange with the topic author is deemed necessary for proposal preparation, that information will be made available to all parties through DSIP Topic Q&A."
- AFTER OPEN: "No further direct contact is allowed between proposing SBCs and topic authors." Written questions only, via DSIP Topic Q&A, answered publicly on a non-attribution basis, typically within seven business days. Q&A "opens on the pre-release date and closes two weeks prior to the topic close date."
- AFTER CLOSE: "Once the proposal submission closes, no communication of any kind is allowed either with the topic author or through topic Q&A regarding submitted proposals."
The practical consequence: the ~3-week pre-release window is the ONLY time you can have a real conversation, and it is the single most valuable fortnight in the SBIR calendar. Watch for topics on the first Wednesday of the month and call immediately.

=== WHERE TO MEET DoD PROGRAM OFFICERS IN PERSON ===
- Defense Basic Research Exchange (DBRE) — the cross-service meeting between DoD basic research program officers and university researchers. Next: 18-20 May 2027, Alexandria, Virginia (announced on basicresearch.defense.gov).
- DARPA Proposers' Days for a specific BAA — the PM presents the program vision and takes questions; attend if one is held.
- Service PO listings are public: ONR at onr.navy.mil/our-research/our-program-officers; AFOSR POs are listed by research area inside the open BAA and the YIP NOFO; ARL TPOCs via the ARL BAA page. Your institution's research development office usually keeps a DoD contact list and can broker an introduction — ask them first; DoD POs respond better to a warm route.
result.funded_examples_source:
Several routes, of unequal quality. Best first.

1) DoD GRANT AWARDS SEARCH ON DIMENSIONS FOR DTIC — https://dtic.dimensions.ai/discover/grant — VERIFIED LIVE 18 Sep 2026 via a rendering browser. This is the best single resource and most applicants do not know it exists. It holds 169,348 DoD grant awards, alongside 621,229 DoD publications, 80,237 patents, 827,963 technical reports and 33,414 presidential budget reports. There is a "Show abstract" toggle, so you can read the actual funded abstracts, and filters for Critical Technology Areas, start year, active year, grant status, researcher, FUNDER, research organization, and research category. Coverage of grants awarded since December 2014. Practical use: filter FUNDER to "United States Department of the Air Force" (or Navy/Army) and read every YIP abstract from the last three cycles before writing yours — award titles are tagged, e.g. "(YIP) ROBUST ONLINE-OPTIMIZATION UNDER SYMMETRY WITH GLOBAL OPTIMALITY CERTIFICATES", Air Force, $150,000, 2026-2029. Funding amounts and periods are shown. For CDMRP, filter funder to "Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs"; CDMRP's own Search Awards page (cdmrp.health.mil/search.aspx) now simply redirects here and points to a "Searching DTIC for CDMRP Awards" filtering guide. CAVEAT: DTIC's own landing page at discover.dtic.mil/grant/ currently says "DoW Grant Awards Search is offline while we fine-tune the user experience" — that banner contradicts the working Dimensions instance; go straight to dtic.dimensions.ai.

2) CDMRP PUBLIC (LAY) ABSTRACT COMPILATIONS — CDMRP publishes annual PDFs of public/lay abstracts for every funded award, e.g. https://cdmrp.health.mil/pdfs/FY22%20CDMRP%20Awards_Public_Abstracts_91123.pdf. Approximately 22,456 CDMRP awards through FY2024. Because CDMRP peer review panels include consumer reviewers, these lay abstracts are the closest thing to a model answer for the Lay Abstract attachment — read a dozen in your disease area before drafting. Programme pages under cdmrp.health.mil/researchprograms also post lists of organizations and PIs recommended for funding after each cycle, plus "information papers" giving that cycle's receipt/funding metrics (how many applied, how many funded) — the DoD equivalent of a success-rate table, and genuinely hard to find otherwise.

3) SBIR.gov AWARDS — https://www.sbir.gov/awards — verified reachable. Cross-agency SBIR/STTR award database filterable to DoD components, with funded Phase I/II abstracts. The route for anyone considering an STTR partnership.

4) USASPENDING.gov — every DoD grant, cooperative agreement and contract by recipient, amount, and awarding office. No scientific abstracts, but the authoritative source for "how much does this program actually give and to whom", and the way to see which offices fund your institution already.

5) DTIC PUBLIC ACCESS — https://publicaccess.dtic.mil/search/ and apps.dtic.mil — FINAL TECHNICAL REPORTS from completed DoD-funded projects. Under-used and arguably the best preparation of all: reading the final report of a project like yours shows you what DoD expected as deliverables, what the transition narrative looked like, and how the work was framed for a defense audience.

6) DoD BASIC RESEARCH OFFICE — https://basicresearch.defense.gov — the cross-service hub for the university programs (Vannevar Bush Faculty Fellowship, MURI, DEPSCoR, HBCU/MI, Laboratory University Collaboration Initiative, Bilateral Academic Research Initiative) with awardee announcements and news items describing funded work. TOOLING NOTE, per house rules: this site returns HTTP 403 to a plain fetch and had to be read with a rendering browser; that is a fetch artefact, not a sign the site is down.

7) DARPA — no public abstract database comparable to the above. Programme pages on darpa.mil describe active programmes and name performers; the Defense Innovation Marketplace (defenseinnovationmarketplace.dtic.mil) carries some programme documentation.

WHAT IS NOT AVAILABLE, AND MATTERS: there is no DoD equivalent of NIH RePORTER's linkage to summary statements, and NO published sample DoD applications analogous to NIAID's sample R01 packages. I could not establish that any university research office publishes complete funded DoD proposals. The practical substitutes are (a) funded abstracts on Dimensions, (b) the final technical report on DTIC, and (c) asking a funded colleague directly — which is normal practice in this community, since DoD awards are not scored competitively against each other in public and there is little reason to withhold. If you are at a university with a research development office, ask whether they hold internal examples; several large research universities keep DoD proposal libraries that are not on the open web.

This is itself a finding: DoD NOFOs carry internal inconsistencies and are amended after posting, so always check the current amendment on grants.gov/SAM.gov rather than an archived PDF.

result.funder_system: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science (DOE SC) — the seven program offices ASCR, BES, BER, FES, HEP, NP and Isotope R&D and Production (IRP), governed by 10 CFR 605 (Office of Science Financial Assistance Program). Assistance Listing 81.049. Two parallel routes: (a) universities/nonprofits/industry apply through Grants.gov under a NOFO; (b) DOE national laboratories and SC user facilities respond instead to "Lab Announcements" (LAB-YY-NNNN) posted in PAMS, not Grants.gov, with Field Work Proposals requested only from those selected. The workhorse mechanism is the annual "Continuation of Solicitation for the Office of Science Financial Assistance Program" (the Open Call) — FY2026 = DE-FOA-0003600, ~$500M, historically 200-350 new awards/yr, $5k-$5M, most commonly 3-year project periods. Named mechanisms on top of it: Early Career Research Program (ECRP, DE-FOA-0003602, ~$875k/5yr academic, ~$2.75M/5yr lab), topical FOAs, and SCGSR for PhD students (3-12 month paid residencies at a DOE lab). FETCH NOTE: science.osti.gov HTML pages fetched normally; the three large PDFs (DE-FOA-0003600-000001, DE-FOA-0003602, ECRP FY2026 FAQ) returned as binary to the fetch summarizer, so I downloaded them and extracted text locally with pdftotext — every PDF quote below is from DOE's own primary document. eCFR blocked the fetch (302 redirect to unblock.federalregister.gov), so the 10 CFR 605.10 wording is quoted from DOE's own reproduction on science.osti.gov, not from eCFR.
result.submission_portal:
TWO portals, and confusing them is the classic first-timer error. (1) FULL APPLICATIONS → Grants.gov only: "Applications in response to this NOFO must be submitted through Grants.gov." and "Applications submitted through www.FedConnect.net will not be accepted. Applications may not be submitted through PAMS." Search by Assistance Listing 81.049 or the NOFO number; use Workspace, downloaded forms, or system-to-system. Proof of timeliness is the Grants.gov timestamp; you get a GRANTXXXXXXXX tracking number, then a second email when SC retrieves it — "SC will have no records of your attempted submission without the second email from Grants.gov." (2) PRE-APPLICATIONS / WHITE PAPERS / LETTERS OF INTENT → PAMS only (https://pamspublic.science.energy.gov/): "Pre-applications ... must be submitted electronically through the DOE SC Portfolio Analysis and Management System (PAMS) website ... You cannot draft or edit a pre-application in PAMS. Do not submit a pre-application through FedConnect or Grants.gov." PAMS is also where you later view merit reviewer comments, submit Renewal Proposal Products, and withdraw an application.

HIDDEN LONG-LEAD REGISTRATIONS (start these before you start writing): SAM.gov + Unique Entity Identifier (12-digit, no hyphens) + EIN/TIN from IRS; Grants.gov with an AOR role authorized by your e-Business Point of Contact; PAMS (two-step: create an individual account, then "register to" your institution — a PI cannot submit a pre-application alone, it needs a user with the "Submit to DOE" privilege, and for ECRP an authorized institutional representative must submit it); FedConnect (needs your SAM MPIN — this is where the binding award documents are posted); FSRS (https://www.fsrs.gov, "must be completed before an award may be made"). DOE's own lead times, quoted: "Applicants not currently registered with SAM and Grants.gov should allow at least four weeks to complete these requirements" and "You are encouraged to register for an account in PAMS at least a week in advance of the LOI submission deadline." Also quoted: "All PIs and those submitting LOIs on behalf of PIs are encouraged to establish PAMS accounts as soon as possible to avoid submission delays." PAMS help desk: 855-818-1846 / sc.pams-helpdesk@science.doe.gov, Mon-Fri 9:00-17:30 ET. Filenames must be ≤50 characters or the application may be rejected.
result.deadline_structure:
DOE SC absolutely does publish dated deadlines — three distinct layers, and only the first is genuinely "rolling".

LAYER 1 — the Open Call is rolling with a hard annual close. DE-FOA-0003600 cover: "This NOFO will remain open until September 30, 2026, or until replaced by a successor NOFO. Applications may be submitted any time during that period." A successor NOFO is issued every year at end of September (DE-FOA-0003600 issued 29-30 Sept 2025; it "succeeds DE-FOA-0003432, which was published September 30, 2024"). Pre-applications: "may be submitted at any time while this NOFO is available."

LAYER 2 — per-topic TARGET DATES inside the Open Call, which is where the real calendar lives. BES states the logic plainly: "These dates are not hard deadlines and applications are accepted throughout the fiscal year for all BES core research areas ... The target dates reflect the time needed to conduct the review and recommendation process for support with funds from this fiscal year. Applications submitted after a target date are not guaranteed consideration for funding this fiscal year." FY2026 actual dates: most BES core research areas — "Pre-applications are strongly encouraged and should be submitted by November 30, 2025" / "Applications submitted by February 1, 2026, will be considered for funding in FY 2026." BES Separations Science — pre-app 31 Oct 2025, application 10 Dec 2025. Several BER/BES topics say "There is no target date for pre-applications." Panel-reviewed topics run a three-step dated gate: ASCR Applied Math — pre-app 14 Nov 2025 → encourage/discourage 15 Dec 2025 → application 16 Jan 2026; ASCR (second topic, panel in March 2026) — 14 Nov 2025 → 18 Dec 2025 → 28 Jan 2026; FES — 25 Nov 2025 → 10 Dec 2025 → 20 Jan 2026, and another FES topic 31 Jan 2026 → (response) → 15 Mar 2026; HEP DUNE — 5 Dec 2025 → 19 Dec 2025 → 30 Jan 2026; HEP QIS — 15 Nov 2025 → 15 Dec 2025 → 1 Feb 2026 with "a start date of July 1, 2026"; HEP blue-sky (panel June 2026) — 27 Feb 2026 → 27 Mar 2026 → 1 May 2026. The recurring SHAPE, which is what a first-timer should internalize: pre-application Oct-Feb → encouragement/discouragement email ~3-6 weeks later → full application Dec-May → panel spring → awards summer/early autumn. Cover text: "Applications submitted after the panel's acceptance date may be held until the next review panel."

LAYER 3 — fiscal-year physics that overrides everything: "Applications submitted in the latter half of the Federal fiscal year (April 1 - September 30) may be considered for funding in the next fiscal year." Two further hard rules: conference/workshop support "must be submitted at least six months before the meeting date and no later than April 1, 2026, to be considered for FY 2026 funding"; renewals "must be submitted through Grants.gov at least six months before the scheduled expiration of the current award's project period."

NAMED MECHANISMS WITH FIXED-ISH ANNUAL CYCLES. ECRP FY2026 (DE-FOA-0003602, issued 3 Mar 2026): pre-application MANDATORY, due "March 24, 2026, at 5:00 PM ET"; encourage/discourage response "April 21, 2026, at 5:00 PM ET"; application "June 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET". Caution on drift: the ECRP month moves — the FY2025 cycle opened 17 Jan 2025, the FY2026 cycle opened 3 Mar 2026 — so treat "March/June" as this cycle's dates, not a fixed rule. SCGSR (for PhD students) runs two cycles a year and DOE publishes them a year ahead: 2026 Solicitation 1 — opens 11 Feb 2026, closes 6 May 2026 (17:00 ET), notification 8-21 Sept 2026, research starts 2 Nov 2026 - 1 Mar 2027; 2026 Solicitation 2 — opens 12 Aug 2026, closes 4 Nov 2026, notification 1-16 Apr 2027, starts 7 Jun - 4 Oct 2027; 2027 Sol 1 tentatively opens Feb 2027, closes May 2027. All times Eastern; Grants.gov/PAMS close at the stated minute.

review_stages.stage: Grants.gov receipt and timestamp; automatic transfer into PAMS
review_stages.timing: Immediate; the Grants.gov timestamp is the legal proof of timeliness. Two confirmation emails follow (Grants.gov receipt, then SC retrieval) — chase the second one if it does not arrive.

review_stages.stage: Responsiveness / initial review by DOE staff under 10 CFR 605.10(b) — eligibility, completeness, technical soundness, responsiveness, non-duplication
review_stages.timing: Days to a few weeks; not separately published. Applications failing it "will not be forwarded for merit review and will be eliminated from further consideration." This is also where an unrevised previously-declined application can be killed.

review_stages.stage: Assignment to an SC Program Manager, who runs the merit review
review_stages.timing: Weeks. For renewals, PAMS emails the PI to complete the Renewal Proposal Products list; "The application will not be considered complete and cannot be sent for review until the product list has been submitted."

review_stages.stage: Merit (peer) review — mail review, panel review, or a combination, decided program by program. Merit Review System: the project manager sends it to "at least three qualified reviewers"; Federal and non-Federal reviewers both used
review_stages.timing: Rolling for the Open Call; for panel topics, a scheduled panel (e.g. ASCR March 2026, HEP June 2026) typically 2-4 months after the topic's application date.

review_stages.stage: Selection Official decision — merit review scores plus Program Policy Factors (availability of funds, relevance to SC and Presidential priorities, portfolio balance, performance under current awards, "Promoting principal investigators not previously supported by SC", "Promoting institutions not previously supported by SC", lower indirect rate, training/mentoring history)
review_stages.timing: Not separately timed. Explicitly NOT score-ranked funding: per the ECRP FAQ, "No, the Selection Official will consider the merit review scores and written recommendations, program policy factors, and the amount of funding available."

review_stages.stage: Notice of Selection for Award Negotiation (and, for the unsuccessful, a declination that states why)
review_stages.timing: Open Call: "DOE anticipates making funding decisions within six months. The time interval begins on the date the application is received." Regulatory backstop (10 CFR 605.10, quoted on science.osti.gov): "Applications shall be evaluated for funding generally within 6 months but, in any event, no later than 12 months from the date of receipt by DOE." ECRP FY2026: "It is anticipated that the award selection will be completed by July 2026" — about 1 month after the 2 June application date.

review_stages.stage: Merit reviewer comments released to the PI in PAMS ("View Reviews")
review_stages.timing: At or shortly after the decision. ECRP FAQ: "Principal Investigators will have access to the reviewer comments in PAMS at the time or shortly after the application is recommended for funding or declined." The Merit Review System adds: "Upon request, applicants/proposers will be provided with a written summary of the evaluation of their application/proposal."

review_stages.stage: Negotiation with the Integrated Service Center, risk review (2 CFR 200.206) and Research/Technology/Economic Security (RTES) due-diligence review, then the Assistance Agreement issued by the Contracting Officer; binding documents posted to FedConnect
review_stages.timing: Weeks to a few months after selection. RTES is "conducted separately from the technical merit review" and "DOE's decision regarding a due diligence review is not appealable."

review_stages.stage: Earliest award start
review_stages.timing: Open Call: negotiated; awards run 6 months to 5 years, most commonly 3 years. ECRP FY2026 FAQ suggests "a start date of September 1, 2026" — i.e. ~3 months after the application deadline — and notes "The date mentioned in an application is not binding." Realistic end-to-end for the Open Call: 6-9 months from submission to money, and longer if you land in the April-September window that pushes you into the next fiscal year.

result.months_submission_to_award: Open Call: DOE's own target is 6 months from receipt to funding decision, with a regulatory ceiling of 12 months; add roughly 1-3 months of negotiation and award issuance, so plan 6-9 months submission-to-start, and up to 12+ if you submit between 1 April and 30 September (those "may be considered for funding in the next fiscal year"). Panel-reviewed topics: ~2-4 months from application to panel, awards typically the following summer — e.g. HEP QIS, application 1 Feb 2026 with "a start date of July 1, 2026" (~5 months). ECRP FY2026: pre-application 24 Mar → decision on the pre-application 21 Apr (~1 month) → application 2 Jun → selection by July 2026 (~1 month) → suggested start 1 Sept 2026 — about 5 months from the pre-application, 3 from the application. Counting from the first real deadline you must hit, an ECRP cycle is ~9-11 months of your life once you include the pre-application drafting. SCGSR: ~4 months application-to-notification, ~6 months to earliest start. DOE does not publish an observed distribution of actual times for the Open Call — only the 6-month target — so treat 6 months as a floor, not a median.
result.resubmission_policy:
There is no NIH-style resubmission at DOE SC, and this trips people up. The FY2026 NOFO is explicit about the form: on SF-424 (R&R) Field 8, "SC does not make use of the Resubmission or Continuation options." Your choices are New, Renewal, or Revision (Revision = supplemental funding to an existing award). So: NO introduction page is required, there is NO "A1" numbering, NO cap on attempts under the Open Call, and NO stated waiting period. Because the Open Call is rolling, a declined application is simply submitted again as a NEW application whenever a NOFO is open.

The real constraint is substantive, not procedural, and it is stated in the program sections. HEP: "Previously declined applications that have not been substantially revised in light of merit reviewer comments may be declined without additional merit review and will not be considered for funding." BER: "Previously declined applications that have not been substantially revised to address merit reviewer comments may be declined without additional merit review." Practical reading: you get your reviewer comments in PAMS, you must visibly rewrite against them, and an unchanged resubmission is discarded at the responsiveness stage without ever reaching reviewers.

WITHDRAWAL (the mechanism you use to fix a submitted application): "Applications submitted under this NOFO may be withdrawn from consideration by using the PAMS website ... Applications may be withdrawn at any time between when the applicant submits the application and when DOE makes the application available to merit reviewers. Such withdrawals take effect immediately and cannot be reversed." After release to reviewers, you must ask the program office. And: "After an application is withdrawn, it may be resubmitted, if this NOFO is still open for the submission of applications." If you simply submit a corrected version instead, mark SF-424 Field 1 as "Changed/Corrected Application"; "SC will usually consider the last submission, according to its Grants.gov timestamp, to be the intended version."

ECRP IS THE EXCEPTION — a hard lifetime cap. DE-FOA-0003602: "Only one pre-application on behalf of a PI may be submitted in any given SC ECRP competition. A PI may not submit an application in more than three SC ECRP competitions. Participation in the competition is defined as submission of a full application that completed the review/decision process. In rare cases, it is necessary to withdraw an application; an application withdrawn prior to it being officially declined will not count as a submission. Likewise, an application declined without merit review by the DOE SC will not count as a submission." Confirmed in the FAQ: a DISCOURAGED pre-application does not burn an attempt, and an ENCOURAGED pre-application you choose not to act on does not burn one either. Prior ECRP winners are permanently ineligible ("If I received an Office of Science Early Career Research Program award previously, am I eligible? No."); prior PECASE winners are eligible. Also ECRP: you cannot move to a different program office after encouragement — "applications will not be moved between program offices after they arrive."
result.page_limits:
FORMAT BASELINE everywhere: US letter 8.5x11, 1-inch margins all round, body text no smaller than 11 pt, machine-readable PDF only ("Do not submit a scanned image of a printed document"), no PDF portfolios/binders, no editable fields or signatures, filenames ≤50 characters.

PRE-APPLICATION / WHITE PAPER: "The pre-application may not exceed three pages ... Figures and references, if included, must fit within the three-page limit." The title page and the list of individuals who should not serve as merit reviewers are EXCLUDED from the three pages. BER additionally wants a "<100 words" BLUF (Bottom Line Up Front) summary.

PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT (SF-424 R&R Other Project Information, Field 7): "The description of the proposed research may not exceed one page (excluding Project Title and list of investigators) ... Figures and references, if included, must fit within the one-page limit."

PROJECT NARRATIVE — there is NO SC-wide limit in the Open Call; it is set per program office, and this is the single most program-specific number:
• ASCR — no page limit stated in the FY2026 NOFO.
• BES — "Applications submitted to BES through this NOFO typically have Project Narratives that are 15 - 20 pages long. If applicants feel that additional pages are needed ... they should discuss the requested increase with the relevant subprogram contact listed in this NOFO prior to submission."
• BER — "Applications with research narratives in excess of 15 pages may pose an undue burden on merit reviewers and may be declined without review."
• FES — "narratives in excess of 10 pages may present an undue burden on reviewers."
• HEP — single institution: "must not contain project narratives in excess of 9 pages per senior/key person"; multi-institutional teams: "9 pages per senior/key person or a total of 30 pages, whichever is less."
• NP — "in excess of 20 pages (with an additional 5 pages per major research thrust or separate task) ... may be declined without review"; reference list "must not exceed 3-pages"; the required student tracking table and (for renewals) the PI contributions list sit at the end and "will not count against the narrative page limit."
• IRP — no page limit stated.
• ECRP (DE-FOA-0003602) — "The Project Narrative must not exceed a page limit of 15 pages of technical information ... Merit reviewers will only consider the number of pages specified"; the optional table of contents does not count.

EXCLUDED FROM / SEPARATE FROM THE NARRATIVE LIMIT: DOE Title Page; Title Page Supplement for collaborative applications; letters of collaboration or access (Appendix 7 — each is exactly two sentences on a mandated template; letters of recommendation or endorsement are forbidden); biosketches and current & pending support (SciENcv Common Forms, "no page limitation for the Biosketch, though some fields in SciENcv have character limitations", same for the CPS Common Form); budget and budget justification. Appendix 5 Synergistic Activities (optional): one page per senior/key person listing "no more than five distinct examples", and the appendix "may not exceed a limit of the same number of pages as senior/key personnel." For-profit applicants add a "not to exceed 200 words" statement on how the work advances basic scientific understanding.

ASSEMBLY RULE that causes rejections: "SC requires that you create one single machine-readable PDF file that contains the DOE Title Page, Project Narrative, all required appendices, and other attachments" attached to Field 8. Do NOT attach appendices separately to Fields 9, 10, 11 or 12 — "these additional attachments will not become part of the application in PAMS." Also: no URLs pointing to supplementary content ("Merit reviewers are not required to access websites"), and use of generative AI must be disclosed "unless the tools were used solely for editing an original draft."
required_documents: SF-424 (R&R) — complete first, it populates the other forms. Field 8 type: New, Renewal, or Revision (supplement). UEI as 12 alphanumeric characters and EIN as 9 digits, no hyphens. Attach NOTHING to Fields 20 or 21.
Research & Related Other Project Information form
Project Summary/Abstract — 1 page PDF, Field 7. Written for public release: it becomes the published award abstract, so no proprietary or sensitive business information.

Project Narrative — ONE single machine-readable PDF, Field 8, containing the DOE Title Page + the narrative + ALL appendices. Suggested structure: Background/Introduction, Project Objectives, (Renewals only) Progress Report, Proposed Research and Methods, plus a timeline naming which personnel do what and when. A Buy America statement must appear within the first two pages if the project touches public infrastructure.

DOE Title Page (inside the narrative PDF) — project title, institution, addresses, lead PI contact, administrative contact, NOFO number, SC program office and technical contact, DOE award number if a renewal, PAMS pre-application tracking number if any, research area, senior/key personnel list, and a per-institution per-year budget table.

Title Page Supplement (multi-institution collaborative applications only) — institutions and their PIs, the lead PI, leadership structure, each institution's facilities/equipment/resources, how students and early-stage researchers will be trained and mentored, and a summary budget table. Does not count toward the page limit.
Appendix 1: Bibliography & References Cited — every reference must list all authors
Appendix 2: Facilities & Other Resources
Appendix 3: Equipment

Appendix 4: Data Management and Sharing Plan (DMSP) — a scored review criterion. Must cover validation/replication, timely and fair public access to all data behind figures and charts at time of publication, repository selection consistent with the NSTC 'Desirable Characteristics of Data Repositories', FAIR principles for data, software and models, open-source licensing with SPDX identifiers, and software development best practices. Required even if no experimental data is expected; not required for conference/workshop-only requests.
Appendix 5: Synergistic Activities (OPTIONAL) — up to five examples, one page per senior/key person
Appendix 6: Transparency of Foreign Connections
Appendix 7: Other Attachment — two-sentence letters of collaboration or access on the mandated template, SC user facility documentation, and (for DIII-D work) a Record of Discussion from the facility

Identification of Merit Reviewer Conflicts — the list of people who should NOT review your application, attached to Field 12 of the R&R Other Project Information form. The NOFO warns this list 'is rarely empty because the instructions contain mandatory inclusions requirements.' Files in Field 12 are not shared with reviewers.

R&R Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) form — with, for every covered individual at prime and subrecipient level, a SciENcv-generated DOE/NNSA-compliant Biosketch Common Form AND a Current and Pending (Other) Support Common Form. These can no longer be attached to the narrative. Together they must disclose all sponsored activities, awards and appointments — paid or unpaid, full/part-time or voluntary, cash or in-kind, foreign or domestic — and identify any connection to malign foreign talent recruitment programs.
Research & Related Budget + Budget Justification (Field L) — use current negotiated indirect cost and fringe rates; justify every cost
R&R Subaward Budget Attachment(s) Form + subaward budget justifications, if applicable
Project/Performance Site Location(s)
SF-LLL Disclosure of Lobbying Activities, only if you have paid someone to influence a federal officer or Member of Congress

RENEWALS ONLY: Renewal Proposal Products entered directly in PAMS (publications, IP, technologies/techniques, databases, software) — the application cannot go to review until this is submitted; plus a Progress Report section inside the narrative
FOR-PROFIT APPLICANTS ONLY: a ≤200-word appendix on how the work advances basic and fundamental scientific understanding

NOT REQUIRED IN FY2026: a PIER (Promoting Inclusive and Equitable Research) Plan. It appears in a great deal of third-party guidance but the string 'PIER' does not occur anywhere in DE-FOA-0003600-000001 — treat any advice telling you to write one as stale.
result.program_officer_norms:
EXPECTED, and in places MANDATORY — DOE SC sits at the NIH end of this spectrum, not the foundation end. The program manager is a named individual listed against each topic in Section III of the NOFO, and you must pick one from a dropdown when you submit a pre-application in PAMS.

The NOFO's own language, by escalating strength: BES — "Prior to submission, applicants are encouraged to discuss their research ideas with the subprogram contacts listed below." FES and HEP topics — "Applicants are strongly encouraged to contact the subprogram contact before submitting an application" (repeated across many topics). FES Public-Private Partnership — "Applicants must contact the relevant subprogram contact listed below before submitting an application under the PPP program." IRP — projects with unusual scope/budget "should first be socialized with the Program Office." Supplements — "Applicants intending to submit an application for supplemental funding are strongly encouraged to consult their DOE Program Manager before submitting." NP sets the tone limit: "Applicants may email subprogram contacts regarding the technical requirements for the application. Administrative questions should be directed to sc.opencall@science.doe.gov."

WHEN IN THE CYCLE: before the pre-application, and then again between pre-application and full application. The pre-application is itself designed as a conversation-opener, not a gate: "Feedback from DOE to the principal investigator is optional, but you are encouraged to use your submitted pre-application/white paper to initiate a discussion with the listed program manager about the appropriateness of the proposed research for this solicitation." And after it: "Applicants are strongly encouraged to inform their DOE Program Manager if teaming arrangements, proposed personnel, topics, or the anticipated title change between submitting the pre-application and when an application is submitted, to ensure that their application is properly linked to their pre-application and that reviewers are properly assigned."

WHAT EXPERIENCED APPLICANTS ACTUALLY ASK: (1) Which subprogram/topic is the right home for this idea, and is it in scope? (the ECRP FAQ blesses exactly this: "Feel free to contact a program manager if you are uncertain about which topic from the solicitation is the best fit for your idea. The program manager can provide informal feedback on your idea and suggest other program areas if the idea does not fit within his or her area."). (2) May I exceed the narrative page guidance? — BES routes this explicitly through the PM. (3) Is this a New or a Renewal? — "If the application requests a significant change in the scope of work, please consult with the Program contact ... to determine if the application should be considered new or a renewal." (4) Is a panel scheduled for this topic, and what is its acceptance date? (5) Is the budget/team size realistic for this subprogram? (6) Which version of my application should count, if there is submission confusion — "Please consult with your program manager to resolve any confusion about which version of an application should be considered."

IMPORTANT LIMIT ON WHAT INFORMAL CONTACT BUYS YOU: "you may formally submit any pre-application you believe fits within the topics described in the solicitation, regardless of the informal feedback you may receive from a program manager. A formal encourage/discourage decision based on topical fit with the solicitation will be issued for every pre-application we receive." So a warm conversation is not permission, and a cool one is not a veto.

WHERE TO SEND WHAT: technical/scientific questions → the named subprogram contact. Budget and eligibility questions → sc.opencall@science.doe.gov (Open Call) or SC.Early@science.doe.gov (ECRP). System problems → Grants.gov 800-518-4726 / support@Grants.gov, or PAMS 855-818-1846 / sc.pams-helpdesk@science.doe.gov.

LOW-RISK WAY IN FOR SOMEONE WHO DOESN'T WANT TO COLD-EMAIL: BES runs recurring public Office Hours (roughly monthly, Thursdays) with divisional introductions, FOA/proposal-writing sessions, user-facility sessions and open Q&A, with slides and YouTube recordings posted afterwards — https://science.osti.gov/bes/officehours. The FY2026 NOFO points at them directly: "Recordings and slides from past BES and SC events provide an opportunity to learn about BES and SC programs." SCGSR runs its own application-assistance workshops and weekly Friday virtual office hours during each solicitation. ECRP NOFOs carry an "Informational Webinar / Office Hours" section.
result.funded_examples_source:
FOUR real routes, in order of usefulness to a newcomer.

(1) PAMS PUBLIC AWARD SEARCH — https://pamspublic.science.energy.gov/WebPAMSExternal/interface/awards/AwardSearchExternal.aspx — no account needed. Grants, cooperative agreements and interagency awards from DOE SC going back to 2014, searchable by PI, institution, sponsoring SC program office, and free-text over the abstracts themselves. This is the DOE equivalent of NIH RePORTER and it is where you go to find out who your program manager already funds, at what size, and in what language. DOE links it from its own Applicant and Awardee Resources page as "Award Search / Public Abstracts".

(2) ECRP AWARD ABSTRACTS BY FISCAL YEAR — science.osti.gov publishes a per-year PDF of the actual funded early-career abstracts, FY2010 through FY2025 (e.g. https://science.osti.gov/ascr/Research/-/media/early-career/pdf/FY20_DOE_SC_Early_Career_Research_Program_Abstracts.pdf, and award lists such as https://science.osti.gov/-/media/early-career/pdf/2022-Early-Career-Research-Program-Awards---List.pdf). For a postdoc or new assistant professor aiming at ECRP, reading five years of abstracts in your own program office is the highest-value hour available.

(3) TOPICAL FOA AWARD LISTS — https://science.osti.gov/Funding-Opportunities/Award — 109+ entries, filterable by program, initiative and year of announcement (1996-2026), each linking a PDF of the selected projects with titles, PIs and institutions (URL pattern /-/media/funding/pdf/Awards-Lists/[YEAR]/[Award-Title].pdf).

(4) YOUR OWN REVIEWER COMMENTS — for anyone who has already applied, the single best "real example" is your own file: PAMS "View Reviews" releases the merit reviews to the PI and the sponsored research office once a decision is made, and the Merit Review System adds that "Upon request, applicants/proposers will be provided with a written summary of the evaluation." Ask a senior colleague in your department to show you theirs; this is the closest DOE analogue to an NIH summary statement.

ALSO: DOE PAGES/OSTI (https://www.energy.gov/doe-public-access-plan) for the publications that came out of funded awards, and USAspending for dollar figures.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST: DOE SC does not publish full funded application texts, and there is no official DOE sample-proposal library. For a complete narrative you need your university's research development office (many keep internal libraries of submitted DOE proposals) or a FOIA request. Note the NOFO's warning that applications "may be made publicly available if an award is made" — so funded narratives are FOIA-reachable in principle.
